question: Negotiation is a common process in business to mainly solve business conﬂicts between both parties. Compromise is a basic negotiation state in which both parties give up something that they want in order to get something else they want more. Compromise usually occurs in unfair parties when there is a ﬁxed pie to be divided up, and whatever one side gets, the other side loses. In compromise situations, neither side gets all of what they really want, but they each make concessions in order to reach an agreement that is acceptable to both. Both parties usually can reach a win-win concept through compromise. However, negotiation cannot resolve all the conﬂicts if one party is unwilling to resolve the problem.
answer: Negotiation is a common process in business to mainly solve business conﬂicts between both parties, and compromise is a basic negotiation state, in which neither side gets all of what they really want, but they each make concessions in order to reach an agreement that is acceptable to both, and both parties usually can reach a win-win concept, although negotiation cannot resolve all the conﬂicts if one party is unwilling to resolve the problem.
question_zh: 谈判是商务活动中的一种常见流程，主要解决双方之间的商务冲突。妥协是一种基本的谈判状态，双方放弃他们想要的东西，以获得他们更想要的东西。妥协通常发生在不公平的各方中，当有一块固定的蛋糕可供瓜分时，无论一方得到什么，另一方都会失去。在妥协的情况下，双方都得不到自己真正想要的一切，但双方都会做出让步，以达成双方都能接受的协议。双方通常可以通过妥协达成双赢的理念。然而，如果一方不愿意解决问题，谈判并不能解决所有冲突。
answer_zh: 谈判是商业中常见的过程，主要解决双方之间的商业冲突，而妥协是一种基本的谈判状态，双方都没有得到自己真正想要的一切，但双方都做出让步，以达成双方都可以接受的协议，双方通常可以达成双赢的理念，但如果一方不愿意解决问题，谈判无法解决所有冲突。

question: More people than ever now work from home for part or all of the week. Such ﬂexibility can seem a good idea, but many people ﬁnd it diﬃcult to manage their time. Working from home in isolation can also prevent people from engaging in the daily interpersonal relationships that working life can oﬀer – which can help creativity and improve our mental well-being. Time is our most precious commodity and a currency to spend. As my own research on lateness has highlighted, time management involves managing complex relationships and conﬂicts within ourselves – as well as with others. But when working from home, temptations abound which can eat up our time. Food is in the fridge or can be bought on a quick trip to the shops. Excitement of all kinds can be easily accessed through social media, websites or games which will arouse, enrage, shock, entertain, amuse or enthrall us. For some, the temptation to use their time “badly”, particularly online, can be very seductive. At any moment there is a delicate balance of power within: between our creative, constructive side and the side that seeks easier gratiﬁcation and mindlessness.
answer: People ﬁnd, when working from home, it’s diﬃcult to manage their time and prevent them from engaging in the daily interpersonal relationships, as the temptations make time be used ineﬀectively, and there is a balance of power within. （40）
question_zh: 现在，每周部分或整个星期在家工作的人比以往任何时候都多。这种灵活性似乎是个好主意，但许多人发现很难管理自己的时间。在家隔离工作还会妨碍人们参与工作生活所提供的日常人际关系，而这有助于创造力和改善我们的心理健康。时间是我们最宝贵的商品，也是消费的货币。正如我自己对迟到的研究所强调的那样，时间管理涉及管理我们自己以及与他人之间的复杂关系和冲突。但在家工作时，诱惑比比皆是，会占用我们的时间。食物放在冰箱里，或者可以快速前往商店购买。通过社交媒体、网站或游戏可以轻松获得各种兴奋，这些兴奋、激怒、震惊、娱乐、娱乐或着迷。对于一些人来说，“滥用”时间的诱惑，尤其是在网上，可能非常诱人。在任何时候，我们的内心都存在着一种微妙的力量平衡：在我们富有创造力、建设性的一面与寻求更轻松的满足和无意识的一面之间。
answer_zh: 人们发现，在家工作时，很难管理自己的时间，也无法参与日常的人际关系，因为诱惑让时间无法有效利用，而且内部存在权力平衡。 （40）

question: If it seems like you’re not getting enough sleep, you’re not alone. People have evolved to sleep much less than chimps, baboons or any other primates studied so far, a new study ﬁnds. Charles Nunn and David Samson are evolutionary anthropologists. They study how humans have evolved to behave the way we do. Nunn works at Duke University in Durham, N.C. Samson works at the University of Toronto Mississauga in Canada. In their new study, the two compared sleep patterns in 30 diﬀerent species of primates, including humans. Most species slept between nine and 15 hours daily. Humans averaged just seven hours of shut- eye. Based on lifestyle and biological factors, however, people should get 9.55 hours, Nunn and Samson calculate. Most other primates in the study typically sleep as much as the scientists predicted they should. Nunn and Samson shared their ﬁndings on online February 14 in the American Journal of Physical Anthropology.
answer: People have evolved to sleep much less than chimps, baboons or any other primates studied so far, and in their new study, the two compared sleep patterns in 30 diﬀerent species of primates, including humans, and most species slept between nine and 15 hours daily, and humans averaged just seven hours of shut - eye, and based on lifestyle and biological factors, people should get 9.55 hours, Nunn and Samson calculate.
question_zh: 如果您似乎睡眠不足，那么您并不孤单。一项新的研究发现，人类在进化过程中的睡眠时间比黑猩猩、狒狒或迄今为止研究的任何其他灵长类动物都要少得多。查尔斯·纳恩和大卫·萨姆森是进化人类学家。他们研究人类如何进化到我们的行为方式。纳恩在北卡罗来纳州达勒姆的杜克大学工作，萨姆森在加拿大多伦多大学密西沙加分校工作。在他们的新研究中，两人比较了包括人类在内的 30 种不同灵长类动物的睡眠模式。大多数物种每天睡眠 9 至 15 小时。人类平均只睡七个小时。然而，纳恩和萨姆森计算出，根据生活方式和生物因素，人们应该获得 9.55 小时的工作时间。研究中的大多数其他灵长类动物的睡眠时间通常与科学家预测的一样多。纳恩和萨姆森于 2 月 14 日在《美国体质人类学杂志》网络版上分享了他们的发现。
answer_zh: 人类进化到的睡眠时间比黑猩猩、狒狒或迄今为止研究的任何其他灵长类动物要少得多，在他们的新研究中，两人比较了包括人类在内的 30 种不同灵长类动物的睡眠模式，大多数物种每天睡眠时间在 9 到 15 小时之间，而人类平均只睡 7 小时，根据生活方式和生物因素，纳恩和萨姆森计算出，人们应该睡 9.55 小时。

question: Banks provide short-term ﬁnance to companies in the form of an overdraft on a current account. The advantage of an overdraft is its ﬂexibility. When the cash needs of the company increase with seasonal factors, the company can continue to write cheques and watch the overdraft increase. When the goods and services are sold and cash begins to ﬂow in, the company should be able to watch the overdraft decrease again. The most obvious example of a business that operates in this pattern is farming. The farmer uses the overdraft to ﬁnance the acquisition of seed for arable farming, or feed through the winter for stock farming and to cover the period when the crops or animals are growing and maturing. The overdraft is reduced when the crops or the animals are sold. The main disadvantage of an overdraft is that it is repayable on demand. The farmer whose crop fails because of bad weather knows the problem of being unable to repay the overdraft. Having overdraft ﬁnancing increases the worries of those who manage the company. The other disadvantage is that the interest payable on overdrafts is variable. When interest rates increase, the cost of the overdraft increases. Furthermore, for small companies, there are often complaints that the rate of interest charged is high compared with that available to larger companies. The banks answer that the rates charged reﬂect relative risk and it is their experience that small companies are more risky.
answer: Banks provide short - term ﬁnance to companies in the form of an overdraft , and it has the advantage of ﬂexibility of using the overdraft to ﬁnance the acquisition of seed for arable farming , because the overdraft will reduce when the crops are sold , but the disadvantages of an overdraft are repayable on demand and the interest payable on overdraft is variable .
question_zh: 银行以经常账户透支的形式向公司提供短期融资。透支的优点是其灵活性。当公司的现金需求因季节性因素而增加时，公司可以继续开立支票并观察透支增加。当商品和服务出售并且现金开始流入时，公司应该能够看到透支再次减少。以这种模式运作的企业最明显的例子是农业。农民用透支来购买耕种种子，或者为畜牧业提供整个冬季的饲料，并在农作物或动物生长和成熟期间提供资金。当农作物或牲畜出售时，透支就会减少。透支的主要缺点是需要按需偿还。因天气不好而歉收的农民都知道无法偿还透支的问题。透支融资增加了公司管理人员的担忧。另一个缺点是透支的应付利息是可变的。当利率上升时，透支成本就会增加。此外，对于小公司来说，经常有人抱怨所收取的利率比大公司的利率高。银行回答说，收取的利率反映了相对风险，根据他们的经验，小公司风险更大。
answer_zh: 银行以透支的形式向企业提供短期融资，其优点是可以灵活地利用透支来购买耕种种子，因为当农作物出售时，透支就会减少，但透支的缺点是需要随时偿还，透支的利息是可变的。

question: The United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has released a new report on anthropogenic climate change. The ﬁndings of the report include the following: The world’s average surface temperature has increased by around 0.74°C over the past 100 years (1906 -- 2005). A warming of about 0.2°C is projected for each of the next two decades. The best estimates for sea-level rise due to ocean expansion and glacier melt by the end of the century (compared to 1989 --1999 levels) have narrowed to 28--58 cm, versus 9--88 cm in the 2001 report, due to improved understanding. However, larger values of up to 1 m by 2100 cannot be ruled out if ice sheets continue to melt as temperature rises. Sea ice is projected to shrink in both the Arctic and Antarctic regions. Large areas of the Arctic Ocean could lose year-round ice cover by the end of the 21st century if human emissions reach the higher end of current estimates. The extent of Arctic sea ice has already shrunk by about 2.7 per cent per decade since 1978, with the summer minimum declining by about 7.1 per cent per decade. Snow cover has decreased in most regions, especially in spring. The maximum extent of frozen ground in the winter/spring season decreased by about 7 per cent in the Northern Hemisphere over the latter half of the 20th century. The average freezing date for rivers and lakes in the Northern Hemisphere over the past 150 years has arrived later by some 5.8 days per century, while the average break-up date has arrived earlier by 6.5 days per century. It is "very likely " that precipitation will increase at high latitudes and "likely" it will decrease over most subtropical land regions. The pattern of these changes is similar to what has been observed during the 20th century.
answer: A documented 0.74°C increase in the Earth 's average surface temperature over the past 100 years is driving a global mean sea-level rise of 28-58 cm due to oceanic thermal expansion and the melting of glaciers, and is further projected to cause substantial future reductions in polar sea ice extent alongside widely observed declines in seasonal snow cover, especially throughout the spring season.
question_zh: 联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会（IPCC）发布了一份关于人为气候变化的新报告。该报告的调查结果包括以下内容： 在过去 100 年（1906 年至 2005 年）中，世界平均地表温度上升了约 0.74°C。预计未来二十年每年气温升高约 0.2°C。由于了解的加深，到本世纪末由于海洋扩张和冰川融化导致海平面上升的最佳估计（与1989年-1999年的水平相比）已缩小至28--58厘米，而2001年报告中的海平面上升为9--88厘米。然而，如果冰盖随着温度升高而继续融化，则不能排除到 2100 年达到 1 m 的更大值。预计北极和南极地区的海冰都会萎缩。如果人类排放量达到目前估计的上限，到 21 世纪末，北冰洋大片地区可能会失去全年的冰层。自1978年以来，北极海冰的范围已经每十年缩小约2.7%，夏季最低值每十年缩小约7.1%。大多数地区的积雪已经减少，特别是在春季。 20世纪下半叶，北半球冬春季节最大冻土面积减少了约7%。过去150年来，北半球河流湖泊平均结冰日期每世纪推迟约5.8天，平均解冻日期每世纪提前6.5天。高纬度地区的降水量“很可能”会增加，而大多数亚热带陆地地区的降水量“很可能”会减少。这些变化的模式与 20 世纪观察到的情况类似。
answer_zh: 据记录，过去100年地球平均表面温度上升了0.74°C，由于海洋热膨胀和冰川融化，全球平均海平面上升了28-58厘米，预计未来将导致极地海冰范围大幅减少，同时广泛观察到的季节性积雪减少，尤其是整个春季。

question: By living in close contact with humans, dogs have developed speciﬁc skills that enable them to interact and communicate eﬀectively with people. Recent studies have shown that the canine brain can pick up on emotional cues contained in a person 's voice, body odor and posture, and read their faces. In this study, the authors observed what happened when they presented photographs of the same two adults ' faces, a man and a woman, to 26 feeding dogs. The images were placed strategically to the sides of the animals ' lives of sight and the photos showed a human face expressing one of the six basic human emotions: anger, fear, happiness, sadness, surprise, disgust or being neutral. The dogs showed greater response and cardiac activity when shown photographs that expressed arousing emotional states such as anger, fear and happiness. They also took longer to resume feeding after seeing these images. The dogs ' increased heart rate indicated that in these cases they experienced higher levels of stress. In addition, dogs turned their heads to the left when they saw human faces expressing anger, fear or happiness. The reverse happened when the faces looked surprised, possibly because dogs view it as a non-threatening, relaxed expression. These ﬁndings, therefore, support the existence of an asymmetrical emotional modulation of dogs' brains to process basic human emotions.
answer: The ﬁndings, including canine brain picking up on emotional cues contained in a person and greater response and cardiac activity when shown photographs that expressed arousing emotional states, support the existence of an asymmetrical emotional modulation of dogs' brains to process basic human emotions.（44）
question_zh: 通过与人类的密切接触，狗已经发展出了特殊的技能，使它们能够与人类进行有效的互动和交流。最近的研究表明，犬类的大脑可以捕捉到人的声音、体味和姿势中包含的情绪线索，并解读他们的面部表情。在这项研究中，作者观察了当他们向 26 只喂食的狗展示同一两个成年人（一男一女）面孔的照片时发生的情况。这些图像被策略性地放置在动物视线的两侧，照片上显示了一张人脸，表达了人类六种基本情感之一：愤怒、恐惧、快乐、悲伤、惊讶、厌恶或中立。当展示表达愤怒、恐惧和快乐等情绪状态的照片时，狗表现出更大的反应和心脏活动。看到这些图像后，他们也需要更长的时间才能恢复进食。狗的心率增加表明在这些情况下它们承受了更高的压力。此外，当狗看到人脸表达愤怒、恐惧或快乐时，它们会将头转向左侧。当人们的表情看起来很惊讶时，情况恰恰相反，可能是因为狗认为这是一种不具威胁性、放松的表情。因此，这些发现支持狗的大脑在处理人类基本情绪时存在不对称的情绪调节。
answer_zh: 这些发现，包括狗的大脑接收到人身上包含的情绪线索，以及当展示表达唤起情绪状态的照片时更大的反应和心脏活动，支持狗的大脑在处理基本人类情绪时存在不对称的情绪调节。（44）

question: A leader can deﬁne or clarify goals by issuing a memo or an executive order, an edict or a fatwa or a tweet, by passing a law, barking a command, or presenting an interesting idea in a meeting of colleagues. Leaders can mobilize people 's energies in ways that range from subtle, quiet persuasion to coercive threats or the use of deadly force. Sometimes a charismatic leader such as Martin Luther King Jr. can deﬁne goals and mobilize energies through rhetoric and the power of example. We can think of leadership as a spectrum, in terms of both visibility and the power the leader wields. On one end of the spectrum, we have the most visible: authoritative leaders like the president of the United States or the prime minister of the United Kingdom, or a dictator such as Hitler or Qaddaﬁ . At the opposite end of the spectrum is casual, low-key leadership found in countless situations every day around the world, leadership that can make a signiﬁcant diﬀerence to the individuals whose lives are touched by it. Over the centuries, the ﬁrst kind, the out-in-front, authoritative leadership, has generally been exhibited by men. Some men in positions of great authority, including Nelson Mandela, have chosen a strategy of " leading from behind more often, however, top leaders have been quite visible in their exercise of power. Women(as well as some men) have provided casual, low-key leadership behind the scenes. But this pattern has been changing, as more women have taken up opportunities for visible, authoritative leadership.
answer: The pattern, in which men exhibit authoritative leadership while women provided casual, low- key leadership, has been changed as more woman have taken up opportunities for visible, authoritative leadership.（28）
question_zh: 领导者可以通过发布备忘录或行政命令、法令、追杀令或推文、通过法律、发出命令或在同事会议上提出有趣的想法来定义或澄清目标。领导者可以通过微妙、安静的说服、强制威胁或使用致命武力等方式来调动人们的能量。有时，像马丁·路德·金这样具有超凡魅力的领导者可以通过言辞和榜样的力量来确定目标并动员能量。我们可以将领导力视为一个范围，包括领导者的知名度和权力。在这一范围的一端，我们有最明显的：像美国总统或英国首相这样的权威领导人，或者像希特勒或卡扎菲这样的独裁者。与此相反的是，随意、低调的领导力每天在世界各地的无数场合中随处可见，这种领导力可以对那些受到其影响的个人产生重大影响。几个世纪以来，第一种领导力，即直接、权威的领导力，通常由男性表现出来。一些身居高位的男性，包括纳尔逊·曼德拉，选择了“更多地从幕后领导”的策略，然而，高层领导人在行使权力时相当引人注目。女性（以及一些男性）在幕后提供了随意、低调的领导力。但这种模式正在发生变化，因为越来越多的女性有机会担任可见的、权威的领导。
answer_zh: 随着越来越多的女性抓住机会发挥明显的权威领导作用，男性表现出权威领导力而女性提供随意、低调领导力的模式已经发生了变化。（28）

question: Gardeners can feed their families and enrich the soil by growing legumes, such as green beans, soybeans, lentils and peas. Legume roots produce their own nitrogen, which is a major fertilizer nutrient needed by all plants for growth. Nitrogen is produced in nodules that form on the roots of legumes, which contain Rhizobium bacteria. The bacteria take nitrogen from the air and convert it into a form the plants can use. When legumes are pulled up in the fall, excess nitrogen from the nodules is left in the soil. The excess organic nitrogen can be used by other plants in the following growing season. It 's considered organic nitrogen because it was produced naturally, making green beans or peas great rotational crops in an organic crop production system. Organic growers prefer organic nitrogen because of its natural origins and because it breaks down slowly in the soil, thus slowly feeding plants throughout the growing season. Synthetic nitrogen fertilizers tend to release nitrogen quickly and are harsher on the environment. Synthetic nitrogen fertilizers are generally applied in split applications during the season to mimic the slow release of organic nitrogen sources. Each speciﬁc legume generally requires a speciﬁc type of Rhizobium bacteria to produce nodules on its roots. Gardeners who have never grown green beans before can purchase small bags of inoculum or bacteria from the most popular vegetable seed catalogs. Before planting beans, open the package and pour in the dust-like bacteria among the seeds. Shake the package and then plant. Nodules will form on the roots as they develop. The bacteria will remain in the soil, making it unnecessary to inoculate the seed next year. Do not apply extra nitrogen fertilizer to bean crops. Doing so makes bacteria in the nodules lazy, encouraging them to stop producing their own nitrogen. Legumes that are particularly popular in the home vegetable garden include lima beans, peas, edible soybeans, lentils and fava beans. In a recent survey, 44 percent of gardeners trained through New Mexico State University's Master Gardener Program said they grew green beans and other legumes in their home gardens. When planting, be sure to purchase appropriate strains of Rhizobium bacteria for each type of legume.
answer: Gardeners can feed their families and enrich the soil by growing legumes because excess nitrogen from the nodules is left in the soil when legumes are pulled up, which can be used by other plants in the following growing season, but each speciﬁc legume generally requires a speciﬁc type of Rhizobium bacteria, so do not apply extra nitrogen fertilizer to bean crops.
question_zh: 园丁可以通过种植青豆、大豆、扁豆和豌豆等豆类植物来养活家人并肥沃土壤。豆科植物的根部会产生自己的氮，这是所有植物生长所需的主要肥料养分。氮是在豆科植物根部形成的根瘤中产生的，其中含有根瘤菌。细菌从空气中吸收氮并将其转化为植物可以使用的形式。当秋季拔出豆类时，根瘤中多余的氮会留在土壤中。多余的有机氮可以在接下来的生长季节被其他植物利用。它被认为是有机氮，因为它是自然产生的，使青豆或豌豆成为有机作物生产系统中很好的轮作作物。有机种植者更喜欢有机氮，因为它是天然来源，而且它在土壤中分解缓慢，从而在整个生长季节缓慢地喂养植物。合成氮肥往往会快速释放氮，并且对环境的影响更大。合成氮肥一般在季节期间分次施用，以模仿有机氮源的缓慢释放。每种特定的豆科植物通常需要特定类型的根瘤菌才能在其根部产生根瘤。以前从未种植过绿豆的园丁可以从最受欢迎的蔬菜种子目录中购买小袋接种剂或细菌。种豆前，打开包装，将种子中的灰尘状细菌倒入其中。摇动包装，然后种植。随着根部的发育，根部会形成根瘤。细菌将保留在土壤中，因此明年无需接种种子。不要对豆类作物施用额外的氮肥。这样做会使根瘤中的细菌变得懒惰，促使它们停止产生自己的氮。在家庭菜园中特别受欢迎的豆类包括利马豆、豌豆、食用大豆、扁豆和蚕豆。在最近的一项调查中，44% 接受过新墨西哥州立大学园丁大师计划培训的园丁表示，他们在自家花园里种植绿豆和其他豆类。种植时，一定要为每种豆科植物购买合适的根瘤菌菌株。
answer_zh: 园丁可以通过种植豆类来养活家人并丰富土壤，因为拔出豆类时，根瘤中多余的氮会留在土壤中，可供其他植物在接下来的生长季节使用，但每种特定的豆类通常需要特定类型的根瘤菌，因此不要对豆类作物施用额外的氮肥。

question: Half a lifetime ago l made lifestyle choice to exchange a city terrace for a farm cottage. l knew it was a good idea because I had been there before. Born and reared on a farm, I had been seduced for a few years by the idea of being a big shot who lived and worked in a city rather than only going for the day to wave at the buses. That also meant l was familiar with some of the minor disadvantages of country living, such as an uncertain water supply, the absence of central heating in most farm houses and a single-track road, easily blocked by snow, broken-down machinery or escaped farm animals. But there were many advantages as I told my young wife back in the mid-Seventies. She might have been hard to persuade as she was town born and bred and eight months pregnant. I was trying to persuade her that exchanging a warm, large town house for a windswept farm cottage on a much lower income was a good idea.
answer: Half a lifetime ago I made a lifestyle choice to exchange a city terrace for a farm cottage, and I knew it was a good idea because I had been there before, although I was familiar with some of the minor disadvantages of country living; there were many advantages as I told my wife back in the mid seventies, but persuading her that country had it over town might have been diﬃcult.
question_zh: 半生前，我选择了将城市露台换成农舍的生活方式。我知道这是个好主意，因为我以前去过那里。我在农场出生和长大，几年来，我一直被一个想法所诱惑，那就是成为一个在城市生活和工作的大人物，而不是只在公共汽车上挥手致意。这也意味着我熟悉乡村生活的一些小缺点，例如供水不稳定、大多数农舍没有中央供暖系统以及容易被雪、损坏的机械或逃跑的农场动物堵塞的单行道路。但正如我在七十年代中期告诉我年轻的妻子的那样，它有很多优点。她可能很难被说服，因为她是在城里出生长大的，而且已经怀孕八个月了。我试图说服她，用收入低得多的方式将温暖的大型联排别墅换成风吹雨打的农舍是个好主意。
answer_zh: 半生前，我做出了一种生活方式选择，将城市露台换成农舍，我知道这是个好主意，因为我以前去过那里，尽管我熟悉乡村生活的一些小缺点;正如我在七十年代中期告诉我的妻子的那样，乡村有很多优势，但要说服她乡村比城镇更有优势可能很困难。

question: The ways of life of Upper Paleolithic people are known through the remains of meals scattered around their hearths, together with many tools and weapons and the debris left over from their making. The people were hunter-gatherers who lived exclusively from what they could ﬁnd in nature without practicing either agriculture or herding. They hunted the bigger herbivores, while berries, leaves, roots, wild fruit and mushrooms probably played a major role in their diet. Their hunting was indiscriminate, perhaps because so many animals were about that they did not need to spare pregnant females or the young. In the cave of Enlene, for example, many bones of reindeer and bison fetuses were found. Apparently, Upper Paleolithic people hunted like other predators and killed the weakest prey ﬁrst. They did, however, sometimes concentrate on salmon runs and migrating herds of reindeer. Contrary to popular beliefs about ‘cavemen’, Upper Paleolithic people did not live deep inside caves. They rather chose the foot of cliﬀs, especially when an overhang provided good shelter. On the plains and in the valleys, they used tents made from the hides of the animals they killed. At times, on the great Russian plains, they built huts with huge bones and tusks collected from the skeletons of mammoths. Men hunted mostly with spears; the bow and arrow were probably not invented until the Magdalenian period that came at the end of the Upper Palaeolithic. Tools and weapons, made out of wood or reindeer antlers, often had ﬂint cutting edges. Flint knappers were skillful and traditions in ﬂint knapping were pursued for thousands of years. This continuity means that they must have been carefully taught how to ﬁnd good ﬂint nodules and how to knap them in order to make knives, burins (chisel-like tools) or scrapers, which could be used for various purposes.
answer: The ways of life of Upper Paleolithic people are known through the remains of meals scattered around their hearths, together with many tools, weapons and the debris, and those people were hunter-gatherers without practicing agriculture or herding, and they did not live deep inside caves, and the tools and weapons were made out of wood or reindeer antlers with ﬂint cutting edges, which shows they must have been carefully taught to do so.
question_zh: 旧石器时代晚期人们的生活方式可以通过散落在壁炉周围的食物残骸、许多工具和武器以及制作过程中留下的残骸来了解。这些人是狩猎采集者，他们完全靠在自然界中找到的东西为生，不从事农业或畜牧业。他们捕猎较大的食草动物，而浆果、树叶、根、野果和蘑菇可能在他们的饮食中发挥着主要作用。他们的狩猎是不分青红皂白的，也许是因为周围有太多的动物，他们不需要放过怀孕的雌性或幼崽。例如，在恩莱内洞穴中，发现了许多驯鹿和野牛胎儿的骨头。显然，旧石器时代晚期的人们像其他掠食者一样捕猎，首先杀死最弱的猎物。然而，他们有时确实会关注鲑鱼洄游和迁徙的驯鹿群。与人们对“穴居人”的普遍看法相反，旧石器时代晚期的人们并不住在洞穴深处。他们宁愿选择悬崖脚下，特别是当悬垂物提供良好的庇护时。在平原和山谷中，他们使用用他们杀死的动物的皮制成的帐篷。有时，在俄罗斯大平原上，他们用从猛犸象骨骼中收集的巨大骨头和象牙建造了小屋。男人大多用长矛打猎。弓和箭可能直到旧石器时代晚期的马格达林时期才被发明。用木头或驯鹿角制成的工具和武器通常有燧石刀刃。燧石敲击者技术精湛，燧石敲击传统已延续了数千年。这种连续性意味着他们必须被仔细教导如何找到好的燧石结核以及如何敲击它们以制造刀、刻刀（类似凿子的工具）或刮刀，这些可以用于各种目的。
answer_zh: 旧石器时代晚期人们的生活方式是通过散落在壁炉周围的食物残骸以及许多工具、武器和残骸来了解的，这些人是狩猎采集者，不从事农业或畜牧业，他们也不住在洞穴深处，工具和武器是用木头或驯鹿角制成的，边缘有燧石刀刃，这表明他们一定是经过精心教导才这样做的。

question: Assessment is a central process in education. If students learned what they were taught, we would never need to assess; we could instead just keep records of what we had taught. But as every teacher knows, many students do not learn what they are taught. Indeed, when we look at their work, it is sometimes hard to believe that they were in the classroom. In fact, it is impossible to predict with any certainty what students will learn as the result of a particular sequence of classroom activities. And because we cannot teach well without ﬁnding out where our students are starting from, we have to assess. Even if all our students started out at the same point (a highly unlikely situation!), each of them will have reached a diﬀerent understanding of the material being studied within a very short period of time. That is why assessment is the bridge between teaching and learning—it is only through assessment that we can ﬁnd out whether what has happened in the classroom has produced the learning we intended. Of course, assessment is also used for other purposes in education, which makes the picture much more complicated. In all countries, assessments of the performance of individual students are used to determine which students are, and which students are not, qualiﬁed for subsequent phases of education, and also to decide which kinds of education students should receive.
answer: Assessment is a central process in education, and as every teacher knows, many students do not learn what they are taught, and furthermore, it is impossible to predict with any certainty what students will learn as the result of a particular sequence of classroom activities, so assessment is the bridge between teaching and learning, and additionally, assessment is also used for other purposes in education. (65 words)
question_zh: 评估是教育的核心过程。如果学生学会了所教的内容，我们就永远不需要评估；相反，我们可以只记录我们所教的内容。但正如每个老师都知道的那样，许多学生并没有学到他们所教的内容。确实，当我们看到他们的作品时，有时很难相信他们是在教室里。事实上，不可能准确地预测学生通过一系列特定的课堂活动会学到什么。因为如果不弄清楚学生从哪里开始，我们就无法很好地教学，所以我们必须进行评估。即使我们所有的学生都从同一点开始（这是极不可能的情况！），他们每个人都会在很短的时间内对所学习的材料有不同的理解。这就是为什么评估是教学和学习之间的桥梁——只有通过评估，我们才能发现课堂上发生的事情是否达到了我们想要的学习效果。当然，评估也用于教育中的其他目的，这使得情况变得更加复杂。在所有国家，对学生个人表现的评估被用来确定哪些学生有资格、哪些学生没有资格接受后续阶段的教育，并决定学生应该接受哪种教育。
answer_zh: 评估是教育的核心过程，正如每个老师都知道的那样，许多学生并没有学到所教的内容，而且，不可能确切地预测学生在特定的课堂活动序列中会学到什么，因此评估是教与学之间的桥梁，此外，评估还可以用于教育的其他目的。 （65字）

question: The Brundtland Report, Our Common Future (1987), deﬁnes sustainable development as "development which meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs' Implicit in this deﬁnition is the idea that the old pattern of development could not be sustained. Is this true? Development in the past was driven by growth and innovation. It led to new technologies and huge improvements in living standards. To assume that we know what the circumstances or needs of future generations will be is mistaken and inevitably leads to the debilitating sense that we are living on borrowed time. Only if we assume that society will remain static can we understand the needs of the future. The way we live today could not have been predicted twenty years ago. The sustainability paradigm fails to recognize this. It is a static view and thus places limits on human ingenuity. Similarly, a whole host of false assumptions dominate environmental thought; the scale of problems is exaggerated, the amount of resources is underestimated and spurious links are made between areas such as green policies and proﬁt, poverty and environmental degradation. Those of us who want a better future need to question these assumptions.
answer: Development in the past was driven by growth and innovation, and it led to new technologies and huge improvements in living standards, and only if we assume that society will remain static can we understand the needs of the future, but the sustainability paradigm is a static view and thus places limits on human ingenuity, and people need to question the false assumptions that dominate environmental thought.
question_zh: 布伦特兰报告《我们共同的未来》（1987）将可持续发展定义为“既满足当代人的需要，又不损害子孙后代满足其需要的能力的发展”。这个定义隐含着旧的发展模式无法持续的想法。这是真的吗？过去的发展是由增长和创新驱动的。它带来了新技术和生活水平的巨大提高。假设我们知道子孙后代的情况或需求是错误的，也是不可避免的。导致我们生活在借来的时间中的令人衰弱的感觉，我们今天的生活方式无法在二十年前被预测到，因此限制了人类的创造力；同样，一系列错误的假设主导了环境思想；问题的规模被夸大了，资源的数量被低估了。我们这些想要更美好未来的人需要质疑这些假设。
answer_zh: 过去的发展是由增长和创新驱动的，它带来了新技术和生活水平的巨大提高，只有假设社会保持静态，我们才能理解未来的需求，但可持续范式是静态的观点，从而限制了人类的创造力，人们需要质疑主导环境思想的错误假设。

question: Ten years ago, Barsky and Purdon (2006) discovered that social networks which are expanding communication through social media are becoming popular and the costs involved are getting further reduced. Yet, library executives did not see how such a phenomenon could become a part of library and information services. They felt that the users should be left to their social media while the library carried on with its traditional roles (De Rosa et al., 2007). This was also the case when Charnigo and Barnett-Ellis (2007) conducted a survey of 126 academic librarians and concluded that 54% of the librarians surveyed did not believe that there was an academic purpose for Facebook. The rationale behind these librarians’ belief was that social media was a space where students interact with each other, hence, the librarian was not welcome as their coming in might be viewed as an invasion of space. But time has proved that as the technology of social media became more popular, users and librarians acquired digital literacy, and libraries, seeing an explosion of social media around it, were forced to reconsider their stance. In a survey involving 497 international librarians, Taylor & Francis (2014) discovered that over 70% of librarians now feel that the use of social media is important. Though the wave began with public libraries (Mon, 2015), today, libraries of every type either have a social media presence or they are seriously considering it. Hence, the use of social media by libraries has become mainstream.
answer: Social networks are becoming popular and the costs involved are getting further reduced, but library executives did not see how such a phenomenon could become a part of library and information services, and as the technology of the social media became more popular, users and librarians acquired digitally literacy, and libraries, were forced to reconsider their stance, so the use of social media by libraries has become mainstream.
question_zh: 十年前，Barsky and Purdon（2006）发现，通过社交媒体扩大交流的社交网络正在变得流行，并且所涉及的成本进一步降低。然而，图书馆管理人员并不认为这种现象能够成为图书馆和信息服务的一部分。他们认为用户应该留在社交媒体上，而图书馆则继续发挥其传统作用（De Rosa 等，2007）。 Charnigo 和 Barnett-Ellis (2007) 对 126 名学术图书馆员进行了一项调查，得出的结论是，54% 的受访图书馆员不相信 Facebook 存在学术目的。这些图书馆员的信念背后的理由是，社交媒体是学生相互交流的空间，因此，图书馆员不受欢迎，因为他们的进来可能被视为对空间的入侵。但时间证明，随着社交媒体技术变得越来越流行，用户和图书馆员获得了数字素养，图书馆看到社交媒体的爆炸式增长，被迫重新考虑自己的立场。 Taylor & Francis (2014) 在一项涉及 497 名国际图书馆员的调查中发现，超过 70% 的图书馆员现在认为社交媒体的使用很重要。尽管这股浪潮始于公共图书馆（2015 年星期一），但如今，各种类型的图书馆要么拥有社交媒体，要么正在认真考虑。因此，图书馆使用社交媒体已成为主流。
answer_zh: 社交网络正在变得流行，所涉及的成本进一步降低，但图书馆管理人员并没有看到这种现象如何成为图书馆和信息服务的一部分，而且随着社交媒体技术的日益普及，用户和图书馆员获得了数字素养，图书馆也被迫重新考虑自己的立场，因此图书馆使用社交媒体已成为主流。

question: What is the solution for nations with increasing energy demands, hindered by frequent power cuts and an inability to compete in the international oil market? For East Africa at least, experts think geothermal energy is the answer. More promising still, the Kenyan government and international investors seem to be listening. This is just in time according to many, as claims of an acute energy crisis are afoot due to high oil prices, population spikes and droughts. Geothermal energy works by pumping water into bedrock, where it is heated and returns to the surface as steam which is used directly as a heat source or to drive electricity production. Source: Energy Information Administration, Geothermal Energy in the Western United States and Hawaii. Currently over 60% of Kenya’s power comes from hydroelectric sources but these are proving increasingly unreliable as the issue of seasonal variation is intensiﬁed by erratic rain patterns. Alternative energy sources are needed; and the leading energy supplier in Kenya, Kenya Electricity Generating Company (KenGen), hopes to expand its geothermal energy supply from 13% to 25 % of its total usage by 2020. The potential of geothermal energy in the region was ﬁrst realized internationally by the United Nations Development Program, when geologists observed thermal anomalies below the East African Rift system. Locals have been utilizing this resource for centuries; using steam vents to create the perfect humidity for greenhouses, or simply to enjoy a swim in the many natural hot lakes. Along the 6000 km of the rift from the Red Sea to Mozambique, geochemical, geophysical and heat ﬂow measurements were made to identify areas suitable for geothermal wells. One area lies next to the extinct Olkaria volcano, within the Hell’s Gate National Park, and sits over some of the thinnest continental crust on Earth. This is a result of the thinning of the crust by tectonic stretching, causing hotter material below the Earth’s surface to rise, resulting in higher temperatures. This thin crust was ideal for the drilling of geothermal wells, reaching depths of around 3000 m, where temperatures get up to 342°C, far higher than the usual temperature of 90°C at this depth. Water in the surrounding rocks is converted to steam by the heat. The steam can be used to drive turbines and produce electricity.
answer: For East Africa , especially Kenya, facing rising energy demands, frequent power cuts and an inability to compete in the international oil market, geothermal energy is the solution, which works by pumping water into bedrock to make steam for heat or electricity, Kenya now gets over 60% power from unreliable hydropower, so KenGen plans to raise geothermal supply from 13% to 25% by 2020, with areas like Olkaria volcano ideal for it .
question_zh: 对于能源需求不断增加、经常停电且无法在国际石油市场竞争的国家来说，解决方案是什么？至少对于东非，专家认为地热能是答案。更有希望的是，肯尼亚政府和国际投资者似乎正在倾听。许多人认为，这一举措来得正是时候，因为高油价、人口激增和干旱正在引发严重的能源危机。地热能的工作原理是将水泵入基岩，水被加热并以蒸汽形式返回地表，直接用作热源或驱动发电。资料来源：能源信息管理局，美国西部和夏威夷的地热能源。目前，肯尼亚 60% 以上的电力来自水力发电，但事实证明水力发电越来越不可靠，因为不稳定的降雨模式加剧了季节性变化问题。需要替代能源；肯尼亚领先的能源供应商肯尼亚发电公司 (KenGen) 希望到 2020 年将其地热能供应量从占其总使用量的 13% 扩大到 25%。联合国开发计划署在国际上首次认识到该地区地热能的潜力，当时地质学家观察到东非裂谷系统下方的热异常。几个世纪以来，当地人一直在利用这一资源。使用蒸汽喷口为温室创造完美的湿度，或者只是在许多天然热湖中享受游泳。沿着从红海到莫桑比克 6000 公里的裂谷，进行了地球化学、地球物理和热流测量，以确定适合开发地热井的区域。其中一个区域位于地狱之门国家公园内的奥尔卡里亚死火山旁边，坐落在地球上最薄的大陆地壳之上。这是由于构造拉伸导致地壳变薄，导致地表以下较热的物质上升，从而导致更高的温度。这种薄薄的地壳非常适合钻探地热井，深度可达 3000 米左右，温度高达 342°C，远高于该深度的通常温度 90°C。周围岩石中的水在热量的作用下转化为蒸汽。蒸汽可用于驱动涡轮机并发电。
answer_zh: 对于东非，尤其是肯尼亚，面临着能源需求不断上升、频繁停电以及无法在国际石油市场上竞争的问题，地热能是解决方案，它的工作原理是将水抽入基岩中产生蒸汽来供热或发电，肯尼亚目前超过60%的电力来自不可靠的水力发电，因此KenGen计划到2020年将地热供应从13%提高到25%，奥尔卡里亚火山等地区非常适合。

question: If you are inspired to take concrete action for global peace and development, take a look at the United Nations Volunteers (UNV) program. Every year, up to 8,000 qualiﬁed and experienced women and men of some 160 diﬀerent nationalities volunteer for at least six months of their lives to help others. These UN Volunteers work in some 130 countries promoting peace, responding to disasters, empowering communities and helping to build sustainable livelihoods and lasting development. UN Volunteers come from dozens of professional backgrounds but all of them are catalysts of positive change. They are encouraged to be creative and entrepreneurial, and foster volunteerism for peace and development both within and beyond their assignments. They work at the heart of communities in partnership with governments, United Nations entities and civil society. Being a UN Volunteer is not a career (you are currently limited to four years of service), but it is rich with opportunities and experience and oﬀers huge personal rewards. As a UN Volunteer, you receive a Volunteer Living Allowance (VLA) which covers basic needs, housing and utilities. Additionally, UNV will provide a settling-in-grant, life, health, and permanent disability insurance, return airfares and a nominal resettlement allowance.
answer: If you are inspired to take concrete action for global peace and development, take a look at the United Nations Volunteers (UNV) program, and every year, many qualiﬁed and experienced women and men volunteer at least six months to help others, and UN Volunteers are catalysts of positive change, and being a UN Volunteer provides opportunities, experience and huge personal rewards, and you will receive a Volunteer Living Allowance and other beneﬁts.
question_zh: 如果您受到启发，想为全球和平与发展采取具体行动，请查看联合国志愿者 (UNV) 计划。每年，来自约 160 个不同国家的多达 8,000 名合格且经验丰富的女性和男性会在生命中至少六个月的时间里志愿帮助他人。这些联合国志愿者在约 130 个国家开展工作，促进和平、应对灾害、增强社区能力并帮助建立可持续生计和持久发展。联合国志愿者来自数十种专业背景，但他们都是积极变革的催化剂。我们鼓励他们发挥创造力和创业精神，并在其职责范围内和之外培养促进和平与发展的志愿精神。他们与政府、联合国实体和民间社会合作，在社区的核心开展工作。成为一名联合国志愿者并不是一种职业（目前服务期限仅限四年），但它充满机会和经验，并提供巨大的个人回报。作为联合国志愿者，您将获得志愿者生活津贴 (VLA)，涵盖基本需求、住房和公用事业。此外，联合国志愿人员组织还将提供安置补助金、人寿、健康和永久残疾保险、回程机票和象征性的安置津贴。
answer_zh: 如果您受到启发，为全球和平与发展采取具体行动，请查看联合国志愿者（UNV）计划，每年，许多合格且经验丰富的男女志愿者至少六个月来帮助他人，联合国志愿者是积极变革的催化剂，成为联合国志愿者提供机会、经验和巨额个人回报，您将获得志愿者生活津贴和其他福利。

question: humanity are food energy ，degradation ，and they are all plant related ，and the climate change increase the stresses ，so the plant research is instrumental ，people should use the advanced technologies in the plant research to solve the problems.
question_zh: 人类的食物能源，退化，都与植物有关，气候变化增加了压力，所以植物研究是有帮助的，人们应该利用植物研究中的先进技术来解决问题。

question: You used to think that being green was a luxury for your company, but climate change has made you realize that you can no longer ignore it. The buzz is about becoming carbon- neutral, but where do you start? Consider your drivers. Do you want to become carbon- neutral for marketing reasons, for ﬁnancial reasons or to help save the planet? Simon Armitage of the Carbon Neutral Company believes: "Your drivers will help you tailor your carbon-reduction program and determine key performance indicators. " This will help build a case for going carbon-neutral. First, measure your carbon footprint, or get a specialist to do it for you. That primarily means taking account of your energy usage and emissions caused by travel. Before you begin, think about whether you 're collecting the right data and whether it 's readily accessible. When implementing any energy reduction measures, ensure you engage with your staﬀ . "It 's much better if your people decide for themselves when it 's sensible for them to travel, " says Armitage. You 'll also need them to participate in switching oﬀ the lights and other energy-saving measures. Set targets and show it 's not a one-oﬀ exercise.
answer: People can no longer ignore being green, and the buzz is about becoming carbon-neutral, and people should start with considering their drivers, and they should ﬁrst measure their carbon footprint, or get a specialist to do it, and people should think about whether they’re collecting the right data and whether it 's readily accessible, and when implementing any energy reduction measures, people should engage with their staﬀ , set targets and show it 's not an one-oﬀ exercise. （75）
question_zh: 您曾经认为绿色对您的公司来说是一种奢侈，但气候变化让您意识到您不能再忽视它。人们热衷于实现碳中和，但从哪里开始呢？考虑一下你的司机。您是出于营销原因、财务原因还是为了帮助拯救地球而想实现碳中和？碳中和公司的西蒙·阿米蒂奇认为：“您的司机将帮助您定制碳减排计划并确定关键绩效指标。”这将有助于为实现碳中和奠定基础。首先，测量您的碳足迹，或请专家为您做这件事。这主要意味着要考虑您的能源使用量和旅行造成的排放量。在开始之前，请考虑您是否正在收集正确的数据以及数据是否易于访问。在实施任何节能措施时，请确保与员工互动。阿米蒂奇说：“如果您的员工自己决定何时出行是明智的，那就更好了。”您还需要他们参与关灯和其他节能措施。设定目标并表明这不是一次性的练习。
answer_zh: 人们不能再忽视绿色环保，人们应该开始考虑他们的驱动因素，他们应该首先测量自己的碳足迹，或者找专家来做，人们应该考虑他们是否收集了正确的数据以及数据是否容易获取，在实施任何节能措施时，人们应该与员工互动，设定目标并表明这不是一次性的行为。 （75）

title_zh: 一种新型学习模怯不可练习
人类智商差您不可练习

In general, no single event can be used to predict a volcanic eruption, and thus many events are usually monitored so that taken in total, an eruption can often be predicted. Still, each volcano behaves somewhat diﬀerently, and until patterns are recognized for an individual volcano, predictions vary in their reliability. Furthermore, sometimes a volcano can erupt with no precursor events at all. After the catastrophic eruption of Mount St. Helens on May 18, 1980, a volcanic dome began to grow in the crater. Growth of this dome occurred sporadically, and sometimes small eruptions occurred from the dome. After several years of dedicated monitoring, scientists are now able to predict with increasing accuracy eruptions from this dome. An example is shown in the graphs to the right. In the weeks prior to an eruption on March 19, 1982, the amount of seismic energy released increased, the amount dome expansion increased, tilt increased, and SO2 emissions increased prior to the event. Note that eruption predictions such as in this example are only possible if constant monitoring of a volcano takes place. Monitoring is an expensive endeavor, and not all active or potentially active volcanoes are monitored. Still, if people living around volcanoes are aware of some of the precursor phenomena that occur, they may be able to communicate their ﬁndings of anomalous events to scientists who can begin monitoring on a regular basis and help prevent a pending disaster.
answer: Volcanic eruptions cannot be predicted by a single event but require monitoring multiple signals, though each volcano varies and some erupt without precursors; after long-term monitoring, Mount St. Helens’ dome eruptions became more predictable, and while monitoring is costly, local people’s observations of anomalies can assist scientists in preventing disasters.
question_zh: 一般来说，没有单一事件可以用来预测火山喷发，因此通常会监测许多事件，以便总的来说，通常可以预测火山喷发。尽管如此，每座火山的行为都有些不同，在识别出单个火山的模式之前，预测的可靠性会有所不同。此外，有时火山可能在没有任何前兆事件的情况下爆发。 1980 年 5 月 18 日圣海伦斯火山发生灾难性喷发后，火山口开始形成火山圆顶。这个圆顶的生长是零星发生的，有时圆顶会发生小规模的喷发。经过几年的专门监测，科学家们现在能够更加准确地预测这个圆顶的喷发。右图显示了一个示例。 1982 年 3 月 19 日喷发前几周，地震能量释放量增加，穹顶膨胀量增加，倾斜度增加，SO2 排放量在事件发生前增加。请注意，只有持续监测火山，才能进行本示例中的喷发预测。监测是一项昂贵的工作，并且并非所有活火山或潜在活火山都受到监测。尽管如此，如果生活在火山周围的人们意识到发生的一些先兆现象，他们也许能够将他们对异常事件的发现传达给科学家，科学家可以开始定期监测并帮助预防即将发生的灾难。
answer_zh: 火山喷发无法通过单一事件来预测，而是需要监测多个信号，尽管每座火山的情况各不相同，有些火山爆发没有前兆；经过长期监测，圣海伦火山的圆顶喷发变得更加可预测，虽然监测成本高昂，但当地人对异常现象的观察可以帮助科学家预防灾难。

question: Ecology is the study of interactions of organisms among themselves and with their environment. It seeks to understand patterns in nature (e.g., the spatial and temporal distribution of organisms) and the processes governing those patterns. Climatology is the study of the physical state of the atmosphere – its instantaneous state or weather, its seasonal-to-interannual variability, its long-term average condition or climate, and how climate changes over time. These two ﬁelds of scientiﬁc study are distinctly diﬀerent. Ecology is a discipline within the biological sciences and has at its core the principle of natural selection. Climatology is a discipline within the geophysical sciences based on applied physics and ﬂuid dynamics. Both, however, share a common history. The origin of these sciences is attributed to Aristotle and Theophrastus and their books Meteorological and Enquiry into Plants, respectively, but their modern beginnings trace back to natural history and plant geography. Seventeenth, eighteenth, and nineteenth-century naturalists and geographers saw changes in vegetation as they explored new regions and laid the foundation for the development of ecology and climatology as they sought explanations for these geographic patterns. Alexander von Humboldt, in the early 1800s, observed that widely separated regions have structurally and functionally similar vegetation if their climates are similar. Alphonse de Candolle hypothesized that latitudinal zones of tropical, temperate, and arctic vegetation are caused by temperature and in 1874 proposed formal vegetation zones with associated temperature limits.
answer: Ecology is the study of interactions of organisms among themselves and with their environment, while climatology is the study of the physical state of the atmosphere, and these two ﬁelds of scientiﬁc study are distinctly diﬀerent, but they share a common history, and previous naturalists and geographers see changes in vegetation as they explore new regions and lay the foundation for the development of ecology and climatology as they seek explanations for these geographic patterns.
question_zh: 生态学是研究生物体之间以及生物体与环境之间相互作用的学科。它试图理解自然界的模式（例如，生物体的空间和时间分布）以及控制这些模式的过程。气候学是对大气物理状态的研究——它的瞬时状态或天气、季节到年际的变化、长期平均条件或气候，以及气候如何随时间变化。这两个科学研究领域截然不同。生态学是生物科学中的一门学科，其核心是自然选择原理。气候学是地球物理科学中的一门学科，以应用物理学和流体动力学为基础。然而，两者有着共同的历史。这些科学的起源可归因于亚里士多德和泰奥弗拉斯托斯及其著作《气象学》和《植物探究》，但它们的现代起源可追溯到自然历史和植物地理学。十七、十八和十九世纪的博物学家和地理学家在探索新地区时看到了植被的变化，并在寻求对这些地理格局的解释时为生态学和气候学的发展奠定了基础。亚历山大·冯·洪堡 (Alexander von Humboldt) 在 1800 年代初期观察到，如果气候相似，相距遥远的地区就会有结构和功能相似的植被。 Alphonse de Candolle 假设热带、温带和北极植被的纬度带是由温度造成的，并于 1874 年提出了具有相关温度限制的正式植被带。
answer_zh: 生态学是研究生物体之间以及与环境之间的相互作用，而气候学是研究大气的物理状态，这两个科学研究领域截然不同，但它们有着共同的历史，以前的自然学家和地理学家在探索新区域时看到了植被的变化，并在寻求对这些地理模式的解释时为生态学和气候学的发展奠定了基础。

Ethics is a set of moral obligations that deﬁne right and wrong in our practices and decisions. Many professions have a formalized system of ethical practices that help guide professionals in the ﬁeld. For example, doctors commonly take the Hippocratic Oath, which, among other things, states that doctors "do no harm " to their patients. Engineers follow an ethical guide that states that they "hold paramount the safety, health, and welfare of the public. " Within these professions, as well as within science, the principles become so ingrained that practitioners rarely have to think about adhering to ethics – it 's part of the way they practice. A breach of ethics is considered very serious, punishable at least within the profession (by revocation of a license, for example) ,and sometimes by the law as well. Scientiﬁc ethics calls for honesty and integrity in all stages of scientiﬁc practice, from reporting results regardless of outcomes to properly attributing collaborators. This system of ethics guides the practice of science, from data collection to publication and beyond. As in other professions, the scientiﬁc ethic is deeply integrated into the way scientists work, and they are aware that the reliability of their work and scientiﬁc knowledge in general depends upon adhering to that ethic. Many of the ethical principles in science relate to the production of unbiased scientiﬁc knowledge, which is critical when others try to build upon or extend research ﬁndings. The open publication of data, peer review, replication, and collaboration required by scientiﬁc ethics all help to keep science moving forward by validating research ﬁndings and conﬁrming or raising questions about results.
answer: Ethics is a set of moral obligations, and many professions have a formalized system of ethical practices, so the principles have become so ingrained that practitioners rarely have to think about adhering to them, and a breach of ethics is considered very serious, and scientiﬁc ethics calls for honesty and integrity in all stages of scientiﬁc practice, and this system guides scientiﬁc from data collection to publication and beyond.
question_zh: 道德是一套道德义务，它定义了我们的实践和决策的正确与错误。许多专业都有正式的道德实践体系，可以帮助指导该领域的专业人士。例如，医生通常会遵守希波克拉底誓言，该誓言除其他外，规定医生“不伤害”患者。工程师遵循道德指南，其中规定他们“将公众的安全、健康和福利置于首位。”在这些职业以及科学领域，这些原则变得如此根深蒂固，以至于从业者很少需要考虑遵守道德——这是他们实践方式的一部分。违反道德被认为是非常严重的，至少在行业内会受到惩罚（例如吊销执照），有时也会受到法律的惩罚。科学道德要求科学实践的各个阶段都保持诚实和正直，从无论结果如何报告结果到正确归属合作者。这一道德体系指导着从数据收集到出版等整个科学实践。与其他职业一样，科学道德深深地融入了科学家的工作方式中，他们意识到他们的工作和科学知识的可靠性总体上取决于对这种道德的坚持。科学中的许多伦理原则都与公正的科学知识的产生有关，这在其他人试图建立或扩展研究成果时至关重要。科学伦理所要求的数据公开发布、同行评审、复制和协作都有助于通过验证研究结果、确认或提出有关结果的问题来推动科学向前发展。
answer_zh: 伦理是一套道德义务，许多职业都有一套正式的伦理实践体系，因此这些原则已经变得如此根深蒂固，以至于从业者很少需要考虑遵守这些原则，违反伦理被认为是非常严重的，而科学伦理要求在科学实践的各个阶段保持诚实和正直，这一体系指导着科学从数据收集到出版及其他领域。

question: Research shows that when people work with a positive mindset, performance on nearly every level — productivity, creativity, engagement — improves. Yet happiness is perhaps the most misunderstood driver of performance. For one, most people believe that success precedes happiness. “Once I get a promotion, I’ll be happy,” they think. Or, “Once I hit my sales target, I’ll feel great.” But because success is a moving target — as soon as you hit your target, you raise it again — the happiness that results from success is ﬂeeting. In fact, it works the other way around: People who cultivate a positive mindset perform better in the face of challenges. I call this the “happiness advantage” — every business outcome shows improvement when the brain is positive. I’ve observed this eﬀect in my role as a researcher and lecturer in 48 countries on the connection between employee happiness and success. And I’m not alone: In a meta-analysis of 225 academic studies, researchers Sonja Lyubomirsky, Laura King, and Ed Diener found strong evidence of directional causality between life satisfaction and successful business outcomes. Another common misconception is that our genetics, our environment, or a combination of the two determines how happy we are. To be sure, both factors have an impact. But one’s general sense of well- being is surprisingly malleable. The habits you cultivate, the way you interact with coworkers, how you think about stress — all these can be managed to increase your happiness and your chances of success.
answer: When people work with a positive mind-set, performance on nearly every level improves, but happiness is the most misunderstood driver of performance, and people who cultivate a positive mindset perform better in the face of challenge, and another common misconception is that genetics, environment or their combination determines how happy we are, but one’s general sense of well-being is surprisingly malleable. (61words)
question_zh: 研究表明，当人们以积极的心态工作时，几乎各个层面的表现——生产力、创造力、参与度——都会得到改善。然而，幸福或许是最容易被误解的绩效驱动因素。其一，大多数人相信成功先于幸福。 “一旦我升职了，我就会很高兴，”他们想。或者，“一旦我达到了销售目标，我就会感觉很棒。”但因为成功是一个不断变化的目标——一旦你达到了目标，你就会再次提高它——成功带来的幸福感转瞬即逝。事实上，恰恰相反：培养积极心态的人在面对挑战时表现得更好。我称之为“幸福优势”——当大脑积极时，每项业务成果都会有所改善。作为一名研究员和讲师，我在 48 个国家观察到了员工幸福感与成功之间关系的影响。我并不孤单：在对 225 项学术研究的荟萃分析中，研究人员 Sonja Lyubomirsky、Laura King 和 Ed Diener 发现了生活满意度与成功的商业成果之间存在定向因果关系的有力证据。另一个常见的误解是，我们的基因、环境或两者的结合决定了我们的幸福程度。可以肯定的是，这两个因素都会产生影响。但一个人的总体幸福感却出人意料地具有可塑性。你养成的习惯、你与同事互动的方式、你如何看待压力——所有这些都可以增加你的幸福感和成功的机会。
answer_zh: 当人们以积极的心态工作时，几乎各个层面的表现都会得到改善，但幸福感是最容易被误解的绩效驱动因素，培养积极心态的人在面对挑战时表现更好，另一个常见的误解是遗传、环境或其组合决定了我们的幸福程度，但一个人的总体幸福感却出人意料地具有可塑性。 (61字)

question: The National Oceanography Center (NOC) is engaged in research into the potential risks and beneﬁts of exploiting deep-sea mineral resources, some of which are essential for low- carbon technology, as well as using ocean robots to estimate the environmental impact of these potential deep-sea mining activities. Late last year the NOC led an expedition on the RRS James Cook that found enough of the scarce element Tellurium present in the crust of a submerged volcano that, if it were all to be used in the production of solar PV panels, could provide two-thirds of the UK 's annual electricity supply. Recently, the NOC also led an international study demonstrating deep-sea nodule mining will cause long-lasting damage to deep-sea life, lasting at least for decades. These nodules are potato-sized rocks containing high levels of metals, including copper, manganese and nickel. They grow very slowly on the sea-bed, over millions of years. Although no commercial operations exist to extract these resources, many are planned. Professor Edward Hill, Executive Director at the NOC commented, "By 2050 there will be nine billion people on earth and attention is increasingly turning to the ocean, particularly the deep ocean, for food, clean supplies of energy and strategic minerals. The NOC is undertaking research related to many aspects and perspectives involved in exploiting ocean resources. This research is aimed at informing with sound scientiﬁc evidence the decisions that will need to be taken in the future, as people increasingly turn to the oceans to address some of society 's greatest challenges. "
answer: The National Oceanography Center (NOC) is engaged in research into the potential risks and beneﬁts of exploiting deep-sea mineral resources, and late last year the NOC led an expedition and found enough of the scarce element Tellurium which could provide the UK 's annual electricity supply, and NOC also found out that deep-sea nodule mining will cause long-lasting damage to deep-sea life, and the NOC is undertaking research related to many aspects.
question_zh: 国家海洋学中心（NOC）致力于研究开发深海矿产资源的潜在风险和收益（其中一些对于低碳技术至关重要），以及使用海洋机器人来估计这些潜在的深海采矿活动对环境的影响。去年年底，国家奥委会领导的 RRS 詹姆斯库克探险队在一座水下火山的地壳中发现了足够的稀有元素碲，如果全部用于生产太阳能光伏板，可以提供英国三分之二的年电力供应。最近，国家奥委会还领导了一项国际研究，证明深海结核开采将对深海生物造成长期损害，至少持续数十年。这些结核是土豆大小的岩石，含有大量金属，包括铜、锰和镍。它们在海床上生长非常缓慢，历经数百万年。尽管不存在提取这些资源的商业活动，但许多活动都在计划之中。 NOC 执行主任爱德华·希尔教授评论道：“到 2050 年，地球上将有 90 亿人口，人们的注意力越来越多地转向海洋，特别是深海，以获取食物、清洁能源和战略矿产。NOC 正在开展与开发海洋资源涉及的许多方面和观点相关的研究。这项研究旨在以可靠的科学证据为未来需要做出的决策提供信息，因为人们越来越多地转向海洋来解决一些社会问题。最大的挑战。
answer_zh: 英国国家海洋学中心（NOC）致力于研究开发深海矿产资源的潜在风险和收益，去年底NOC率领的一次考察发现了足够的稀有元素碲，可以提供英国每年的电力供应，并且NOC还发现深海结核开采会对深海生物造成长期持续的损害，NOC正在开展多方面的相关研究。

question: A day would come, Percy Shelley predicted in 1813, when "the monopolizing eater of animal ﬂesh would no longer destroy his constitution by eating an acre at a meal ". He explained: "The quantity of nutritious vegetable matter consumed in fattening the carcass of an ox would aﬀord 10 times the sustenance if gathered immediately from the bosom of the earth. " Two hundred years later, mainstream agronomists and dietitians have caught up with the poet. A growing scientiﬁc consensus agrees that feeding cereals and beans to animals is an ineﬃcient and extravagant way to produce human food, that there is a limited amount of grazing land, and that the world will be hard-pressed to supply a predicted population of 9 billion people with a diet as rich in meat as the industrialized world currently enjoys, and that it’s not a very healthy diet anyway. On top of this, livestock contribute signiﬁcantly towards global warming, generating 14.5% of all manmade greenhouse gas emissions, according to one much-quoted estimate from the United Nations. Now that the problem has been identiﬁed, the challenge is to persuade people in wealthy countries to eat less meat. That might seem a tall order, but governments have successfully persuaded people to quit smoking through a combination of public information, regulation and taxation.
answer: Percy Shelley predicted in 1813 that the monopolizing eater of animal ﬂesh would no longer destroy his constitution by eating an acre at a meal, which is agreed by mainstream agronomists and dietitians, and livestock contribute signiﬁcantly towards global warming, so the problem identiﬁed is to persuade people in wealthy countries to eat less meat. （55）
question_zh: 珀西·雪莱 (Percy Shelley) 在 1813 年预测，总有一天，“垄断动物肉的吃者将不再因为一顿饭吃一英亩而破坏他的体质”。他解释说：“如果立即从大地深处采集，在养肥一头牛时所消耗的有营养的植物物质的数量可以提供十倍的食物。” 200年后，主流农学家和营养学家已经追上了诗人的脚步。越来越多的科学共识认为，用谷物和豆类喂养动物是生产人类食物的一种低效且奢侈的方式，牧场面积有限，而且世界将很难为预计的 90 亿人口提供工业化国家目前所享受的富含肉类的饮食，而且这也不是一种非常健康的饮食。除此之外，根据联合国一项被广泛引用的估计，畜牧业对全球变暖做出了重大贡献，其产生的温室气体排放量占所有人造温室气体排放量的 14.5%。既然问题已经确定，那么挑战就是说服富裕国家的人们少吃肉。这似乎是一项艰巨的任务，但政府通过公共信息、监管和税收的结合，成功说服人们戒烟。
answer_zh: 珀西·雪莱在 1813 年预测，一餐吃一英亩的动物肉的垄断者将不再破坏他的体质，这一点得到了主流农学家和营养学家的同意，而且牲畜对全球变暖有重大贡献，因此确定的问题是说服富裕国家的人们少吃肉。 （55）

question: Working nine to ﬁve for a single employer bears little resemblance to the way a substantial share of the workforce makes a living today. Millions of people assemble various income streams and work independently, rather than in structured payroll jobs. This is hardly a new phenomenon, yet it has never been well measured in oﬃcial statistics—and the resulting data gaps prevent a clear view of a large share of labor-market activity. To better understand the independent workforce and what motivates the people who participate in it, the McKinsey Global Institute surveyed some 8,000 respondents across Europe and the United States. We asked about their income in the past 12 months—encompassing primary work, as well as any other income-generating activities—and about their professional satisfaction and aspirations for work in the future. The resulting report, Independent Work: Choice, necessity, and the gig economy, ﬁnds that up to 162 million people in Europe and the United States—or 20 to 30 percent of the working-age population—engage in some form of independent work. While demographically diverse, independent workers largely ﬁt into four segments (exhibit): free agents, who actively choose independent work and derive their primary income from it; casual earners, who use independent work for supplemental income and do so by choice; reluctant, who make their primary living from independent work but would prefer traditional jobs; and the ﬁnancially strapped, who do supplemental independent work out of necessity.
answer: Millions of people assemble various income streams and work independently, but it has never been well measured in oﬃcial statistics, and the resulting report ﬁnds that up to 162 million people in Europe and the United States engage in some form of independent work, and independent workers largely ﬁt into four segments including free agents, casual earners, reluctants, and the ﬁnancially strapped.(62)
question_zh: 朝九晚五为单一雇主工作与当今大部分劳动力的谋生方式几乎没有相似之处。数百万人汇集各种收入来源并独立工作，而不是从事结构化工资工作。这并不是一个新现象，但官方统计数据从未对其进行过很好的衡量——由此产生的数据差距阻碍了对劳动力市场活动的很大一部分的清晰了解。为了更好地了解独立劳动力以及参与其中的人员的动力，麦肯锡全球研究所对欧洲和美国的约 8,000 名受访者进行了调查。我们询问了他们过去 12 个月的收入（包括主要工作以及任何其他创收活动）以及他们的职业满意度和对未来工作的愿望。由此产生的报告《独立工作：选择、必要性和零工经济》发现，欧洲和美国有多达 1.62 亿人（即劳动年龄人口的 20% 至 30%）从事某种形式的独立工作。虽然人口结构多样化，但独立工作者主要分为四个部分（如图所示）： 自由代理人，他们积极选择独立工作并从中获得主要收入；临时工，他们通过独立工作来获得补充收入，并且是自愿这样做的；不愿意，他们以独立工作为主要生计，但更喜欢传统工作；以及经济拮据的人，他们出于必要而做补充性的独立工作。
answer_zh: 数百万人汇集各种收入流并独立工作，但官方统计数据从未对其进行过很好的衡量，最终的报告发现，欧洲和美国有多达 1.62 亿人从事某种形式的独立工作，而独立工人主要分为四个部分，包括自由职业者、临时工、不情愿的人和经济拮据的人。(62)

question: Humans love to complain to each other. It helps us feel less alone. Think about what happens when a family member or friend is going through a tough time; they call up someone who will listen to their tale of woe. Unfortunately, negative bonding is the default for many groups. In some families complaining is the only way to get attention. When one person says, I had a bad day; the other person has to top it. "You think you had a tough day, I had to do three TPS reports! " The same thing happens at work and in social settings. "Your child didn 't sleep through the night until 6 months? Mine was a full year old before she went over six hours. " It 's a race to the bottom, the worst situation wins. In Bitching is Bonding, A Guide To Mutual Complaint, Irene S. Levine, Ph.D., a professor of psychiatry at the NYU Langone School of Medicine says, "The reason these conversations feel good is that we feel understood. " People raised in negative environments learn early on, that being positive gets you thrown out of the club. When family dinner is a complaint fest, you’re not going to risk alienation by saying, "Wow, I had an awesome day, don 't you just love life? " Translate this in a work setting, people, often unconsciously, believe being positive keeps you out of the cool club. When negativity provides bonding, humans are reluctant to abandon the behavior that brings them comfort.
answer: Humans love to complain to each other, and it helps us feel less alone, and negative bonding is the default for many groups, and the reason these conversations feel good is that we feel understood, and in a work setting, people often unconsciously believe being positive keeps you out of the cool club, and when negativity provides bonding, humans are reluctant to abandon the behavior that brings them comfort.
question_zh: 人类喜欢互相抱怨。它帮助我们减少孤独感。想想当家人或朋友经历困难时期时会发生什么；他们打电话给愿意听他们悲伤故事的人。不幸的是，消极的联系是许多群体的默认选择。在一些家庭中，抱怨是引起关注的唯一途径。当一个人说“我今天过得很糟糕”时；另一个人必须超越它。 “你认为你今天过得很艰难，我必须做三份 TPS 报告！”同样的事情也发生在工作和社交场合。 “你的孩子直到六个月才睡整晚觉？我的孩子已经一岁了，才睡了六个多小时。”这是一场逐底竞争，最坏的情况获胜。纽约大学兰格尼医学院精神病学教授艾琳·S·莱文博士在《互相抱怨指南》一书中说，“抱怨是联系，相互抱怨指南”，“这些对话感觉良好的原因是我们感到被理解。”在消极环境中长大的人很早就知道，积极的态度会让你被赶出俱乐部。当家庭晚餐是一场抱怨盛宴时，你不会冒着被疏远的风险说：“哇，我度过了美好的一天，你不是热爱生活吗？”将这句话翻译到工作环境中，人们常常无意识地相信积极的态度会让你远离酷俱乐部。当消极情绪提供联系时，人们不愿意放弃给他们带来安慰的行为。
answer_zh: 人类喜欢互相抱怨，这可以帮助我们减少孤独感，而消极的联系是许多群体的默认行为，这些对话感觉良好的原因是我们感觉被理解，在工作环境中，人们常常无意识地认为积极的态度会让你远离酷俱乐部，而当消极情绪提供联系时，人们不愿意放弃给他们带来安慰的行为。

"Over the years, language teachers have alternated between favoring teaching approaches that focus primarily on language use and those that focus on language forms or analysis. The alternation has been due to a fundamental disagreement concerning whether one learns to communicate in a second language by communicating in that language (such as in an immersion experience) or whether one learns to communicate in a second language by learning the lexicogrammar - the words and grammatical structures - of the target language. In other words, the argument has been about two diﬀerent means of achieving the same end. " As with any enduring controversy, the matter is not easily resolved. For one thing, there is evidence to support both points of view. It is not uncommon to ﬁnd learners who, for whatever reason, ﬁnd themselves in a new country or a new region of their own country, who need to learn a new language, and who do so without the beneﬁt of formal instruction. If they are postpubescent, they may well retain an accent of some kind, but they can pick up enough language to satisfy their communicative needs. In fact, some are natural acquirers who become highly proﬁcient in this manner. In contrast, there are learners whose entire exposure to the new language comes in the form of classroom instruction in lexicogrammar. Yet they too achieve a measure of communicative proﬁciency, and certain of these learners become highly proﬁcient as well. What we can infer from this is that humans are amazingly versatile learners and that some people have a natural aptitude for acquiring languages and will succeed no matter what the circumstances.
answer: Language teachers alternate between two teaching approaches: primarily focusing on language use or forms, which cannot be solved easily because both approaches can be supported by evidence, no matter people pick up languages for communicative needs or sit in a classroom setting, and in conclusion, humans are versatile learners and some people have a natural aptitude for acquiring languages and succeed under diﬀerent circumstances.
question_zh: “多年来，语言教师一直在偏爱主要关注语言使用的教学方法和注重语言形式或分析的教学方法之间交替。这种交替是由于对于一个人是否通过用第二语言进行交流（例如在沉浸式体验中）来学习用第二语言进行交流，或者一个人是否通过学习目标语言的词汇语法（单词和语法结构）来学习用第二语言进行交流存在根本性分歧。换句话说，争论是关于两种不同的方式与任何持久的争议一样，这个问题并不容易解决。一方面，有证据支持这两种观点。学习者无论出于何种原因，发现自己身处一个新的国家或自己国家的一个新地区，需要学习一门新语言，并且在没有正规指导的情况下这样做，这种情况并不罕见。如果他们处于青春期后，他们很可能会保留某种口音，但他们可以掌握足够的语言来满足他们的交流需求。事实上，有些人是天生的收购者，他们非常擅长这种方式。相比之下，有些学习者对新语言的全部接触都是以词汇语法课堂教学的形式进行的。然而，他们也达到了一定程度的沟通熟练程度，并且其中某些学习者也变得非常熟练。我们可以从中推断出，人类是惊人的多才多艺的学习者，有些人具有学习语言的天赋，无论在什么情况下都会成功。
answer_zh: 语言教师交替使用两种教学方法：主要关注语言的使用或形式，这很难解决，因为这两种方法都有证据支持，无论人们出于交际需要而学习语言，还是坐在教室里，总之，人类是多才多艺的学习者，有些人具有习得语言的天赋，并在不同情况下取得成功。

question: IN 1953 B.F. Skinner visited his daughter’s maths class. The Harvard psychologist found every pupil learning the same topic in the same way at the same speed. A few days later he built his ﬁrst "teaching machine ", which let children tackle questions at their own pace. By the mid-1960s similar gizmos were being ﬂogged by door-to-door salesmen. Within a few years, though, enthusiasm for them had ﬁzzled out. Since then education technology (edtech) has repeated the cycle of hype and ﬂop, even as computers have reshaped almost every other part of life. One reason is the conservatism of teachers and their unions. But another is that the brain-stretching potential of edtech has remained unproven. Today, however, Skinner’s heirs are forcing the sceptics to think again (see article). Backed by billionaire techies such as Mark Zuckerberg and Bill Gates, schools around the world are using new software to "personalize " learning. This could help hundreds of millions of children stuck in dismal classes—but only if edtech boosters can resist the temptation to revive harmful ideas about how children learn. To succeed, edtech must be at the service of teaching, not the other way around. The conventional model of schooling emerged in Prussia in the 18th century. Alternatives have so far failed to teach as many children as eﬃciently. Classrooms, hierarchical year-groups, standardized curriculums and ﬁxed timetables are still the norm for most of the world’s nearly 1.5bn schoolchildren.
answer: In 1953, B.F. Skinner invented the ﬁrst teaching machine due to uniform education, yet early edtech later failed because of teacher conservatism and unproven eﬀects; although traditional Prussian-style schooling remains dominant, modern personalized education supported by tech billionaires is challenging skeptics, but it should serve teaching rather than replace it to avoid harmful ideas.
question_zh: 1953 年，B.F. 斯金纳 (B.F. Skinner) 参观了他女儿的数学课。这位哈佛大学心理学家发现每个学生都以相同的方式、相同的速度学习相同的主题。几天后，他建造了他的第一台“教学机器”，让孩子们按照自己的节奏解决问题。到了 20 世纪 60 年代中期，类似的小玩意儿已经被挨家挨户推销。然而几年之内，人们对它们的热情就消失了。从那时起，教育技术（edtech）不断重复炒作和失败的循环，尽管计算机已经重塑了生活的几乎所有其他部分。原因之一是教师及其工会的保守主义。但另一个问题是，教育科技的脑力拓展潜力尚未得到证实。然而今天，斯金纳的继承人迫使怀疑者重新思考（见文章）。在马克·扎克伯格和比尔·盖茨等亿万富翁技术人员的支持下，世界各地的学校正在使用新软件来“个性化”学习。这可以帮助数亿陷入沉闷课堂的儿童——但前提是教育科技的推动者能够抵制复兴有关儿童学习方式的有害观念的诱惑。为了取得成功，教育科技必须为教学服务，而不是相反。传统的学校教育模式于 18 世纪在普鲁士出现。迄今为止，替代方案未能有效地教育尽可能多的孩子。对于世界上近 15 亿学童中的大多数人来说，教室、分层年级、标准化课程和固定时间表仍然是常态。
answer_zh: 1953年，B.F.斯金纳因统一教育而发明了第一台教学机器，但早期的教育技术后来因教师保守主义和未经证实的效果而失败；尽管传统的普鲁士式学校教育仍然占主导地位，但由科技亿万富翁支持的现代个性化教育正在挑战怀疑论者，但它应该为教学服务，而不是取代教学，以避免有害的想法。

question: The advantages and disadvantages of solar power compared to other forms of renewable energy have been greatly debated. While obviously superior to some forms of energy, solar power 's high cost and eﬃciency dependent on geography have limited its appeal. However, a large number of advantages also merit further development and even possible adaptation for residences. Advantages of Solar Power Solar energy remains popular because it is both a renewable and clean source of energy. These advantages along with the hope that eventually ,nations can use solar power to decrease global warming ensure its popularity. Renewable Solar energy is a true renewable resource. All areas of the world have the ability to collect some amount of solar power and solar power is available for collection each day. Clean Solar energy is non-polluting. It does not create greenhouse gases, such as oil-based energy does, nor does it create waste that must be stored, such as nuclear energy. It is also far quieter to create and harness, drastically reducing the noise pollution required to convert energy to a useful form. Residential size solar energy systems also have very little impact on the surrounding environment, in contrast with other renewable energy sources such as wind and hydroelectric power. Low Maintenance Solar panels have no moving parts and require very little maintenance beyond regular cleaning. Without moving parts to break and replace, after the initial costs of installing the panels, maintenance and repair costs are very reasonable.
answer: The advantages and disadvantages of solar power compared to other forms of renewable energy have been greatly debated, and solar energy remains popular because it is both a renewable and clean source of energy, and furthermore, solar panels have no moving parts and require very little maintenance beyond regular cleaning.
question_zh: 与其他形式的可再生能源相比，太阳能的优点和缺点一直存在很大争议。虽然太阳能明显优于某些形式的能源，但其高成本和依赖于地理位置的效率限制了其吸引力。然而，许多优点也值得进一步开发，甚至可能适应住宅。太阳能的优点 太阳能仍然很受欢迎，因为它既是可再生的清洁能源。这些优势以及各国最终能够利用太阳能来减少全球变暖的希望确保了其普及。可再生太阳能是一种真正的可再生资源。世界所有地区都有能力收集一定量的太阳能，并且每天都有太阳能可供收集。清洁太阳能无污染。它不会像石油能源那样产生温室气体，也不会像核能那样产生必须储存的废物。它的制造和利用也更加安静，大大减少了将能源转化为有用形式所需的噪音污染。与风能和水力发电等其他可再生能源相比，住宅规模的太阳能系统对周围环境的影响也很小。维护成本低 太阳能电池板没有活动部件，除了定期清洁外，几乎不需要维护。无需损坏和更换移动部件，在安装面板的初始成本之后，维护和修理成本非常合理。
answer_zh: 与其他形式的可再生能源相比，太阳能的优点和缺点一直备受争议，太阳能仍然很受欢迎，因为它既是可再生的清洁能源，而且，太阳能电池板没有移动部件，除了定期清洁之外几乎不需要维护。

question: As a philosopher, mathematician, educator, social critic and political activist, Bertrand Russell authored over 70 books and thousands of essays and letters addressing a myriad of topics. Awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950, Russell was a ﬁne literary stylist, one of the foremost logicians ever, and a gadﬂy for improving the lives of men and women. He was arguably the greatest philosopher of the 20th century and the greatest logician since Aristotle. Analytic philosophy, the dominant philosophy of the twentieth century, owes its existence more to Russell than to any other philosopher. And the system of logic developed by Russell and A.N. Whitehead, based on earlier work by Dedekind, Cantor, Frege, and Peano, broke logic out of its Aristotelian straitjacket. He was also one of the century's leading public intellectuals and won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1950, "in recognition of his varied and signiﬁcant writings in which he champions humanitarian ideals and freedom of thought. " Russell was involved, often passionately, in numerous social and political controversies of his time. For example, he supported suﬀragists, free thought in religion and morals, and world government; he opposed World War I and the Vietnam War, nationalism, and political persecution. He was jailed in 1918 for anti-war views and in 1961 for his anti- nuclear weapons stance. He was married 4 times and had 3 children. With Dora Russell, he founded the experimental Beacon Hill School. He knew or worked with many of the most prominent ﬁgures in late 19th and 20th century philosophy, mathematics, science, literature, and politics.
answer: Bertrand Russell, a distinguished philosopher, mathematician, educator, social critic and political activist who wrote over 70 books and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950, was a towering ﬁgure in analytic philosophy and modern logic; he actively participated in various social and political causes, was imprisoned twice for his beliefs, founded a school, and had interactions with many eminent ﬁgures.
question_zh: 作为哲学家、数学家、教育家、社会批评家和政治活动家，伯特兰·罗素撰写了 70 多本书以及数千篇涉及无数主题的论文和信件。罗素于 1950 年获得诺贝尔文学奖，他是一位优秀的文学文体家、有史以来最重要的逻辑学家之一，也是改善男人和女人生活的牛虻。他可以说是20世纪最伟大的哲学家，也是自亚里士多德以来最伟大的逻辑学家。分析哲学是二十世纪的主导哲学，它的存在更多地归功于罗素，而不是任何其他哲学家。 Russell 和 A.N. 开发的逻辑系统怀特海以戴德金德、康托尔、弗雷格和皮亚诺早期著作为基础，打破了亚里士多德式的束缚。他也是本世纪最杰出的公共知识分子之一，并于 1950 年荣获诺贝尔文学奖，“以表彰他在著作中倡导人道主义理想和思想自由的丰富多彩的重要著作。”罗素经常热情地卷入他那个时代的众多社会和政治争议。例如，他支持妇女参政论、宗教和道德自由思想以及世界政府；他反对第一次世界大战和越南战争、民族主义和政治迫害。 1918 年，他因反战观点而入狱，1961 年因反核武器立场而入狱。他结过4次婚，育有3个孩子。他与多拉·拉塞尔 (Dora Russell) 共同创办了实验性灯塔山学校 (Beacon Hill School)。他认识 19 世纪末和 20 世纪哲学、数学、科学、文学和政治领域的许多最著名的人物，或与他们共事。
answer_zh: 伯特兰·罗素是一位杰出的哲学家、数学家、教育家、社会批评家和政治活动家，着有70多部著作，并于1950年获得诺贝尔文学奖，是分析哲学和现代逻辑领域的杰出人物。他积极参与各种社会政治事业，因信仰两次入狱，创办学校，并与许多知名人士交往。

Skipping Breakfast Has Drawbacks - It’s no mystery why so many people routinely skip breakfast: bad timing. It comes at a time when folks can be more occupied with matters of grooming, attire and otherwise making themselves presentable for a new day. However, studies conducted both in the United States and internationally have shown that skipping breakfast can aﬀect learning, memory and physical well-being. Students who skip breakfast are not as eﬃcient at selecting critical information for problem-solving as their peers who have had breakfast. For schoolchildren, skipping breakfast diminishes the ability to recall and use newly acquired information, verbal ﬂuency, and control of attention, according to Ernesto Pollitt, a UC Davis professor of pediatrics whose research focuses on the inﬂuence of breakfast on mental and physical performance. Skipping breakfast can impair thinking in adults, also. For both children and adults, a simple bowl of cereal with milk goes a long way toward providing a suﬃciently nutritious start to the day. Green-Burgeson recommends choosing a cereal that’s low in sugar — less than ﬁve grams per serving — and using nonfat or one percent milk. Frederick Hirshburg, a pediatrician at UC Davis Medical Group, Carmichael, says that babies and other preschoolers rarely skip breakfast because “they’re usually the hungriest at the beginning of the day. Breakfast then becomes more of a "learned experience " than a response to a biological need, Hirshburg says.
answer: Studies have shown that skipping breakfast can aﬀect learning, memory and physical well- being for both children and adults, and breakfast is more of a "learned experience " than a response to a biological need.(35)
question_zh: 不吃早餐有缺点 - 为什么这么多人经常不吃早餐并不神秘：时机不好。在这个时候，人们可以更加专注于打扮、着装和其他让自己在新的一天变得漂亮的事情。然而，在美国和国际上进行的研究表明，不吃早餐会影响学习、记忆和身体健康。不吃早餐的学生在选择解决问题的关键信息方面不如吃早餐的同龄人那么有效。加州大学戴维斯分校儿科教授埃内斯托·波利特（Ernesto Pollitt）表示，对于小学生来说，不吃早餐会降低他们回忆和使用新获得信息的能力、语言流畅性和注意力控制能力，他的研究重点是早餐对心理和身体表现的影响。不吃早餐也会损害成年人的思维。对于儿童和成人来说，一碗简单的麦片加牛奶对于为新的一天提供足够营养的开始大有帮助。 Green-Burgeson 建议选择低糖麦片——每份含糖量低于五克——并使用脱脂或百分之一的牛奶。加州大学戴维斯分校卡迈克尔医疗集团的儿科医生弗雷德里克·赫什伯格 (Frederick Hirshburg) 表示，婴儿和其他学龄前儿童很少不吃早餐，因为“他们通常在一天开始时最饿。赫什伯格说，早餐更多地成为一种“习得的经验”，而不是对生物需求的反应。
answer_zh: 研究表明，不吃早餐会影响儿童和成人的学习、记忆和身体健康，而且早餐更多的是一种“学到的经验”，而不是对生物需求的反应。(35)

question: It’s important to realize that the brain doesn’t see the world around it simply as though the scene was projected onto a cinema screen on the inside of your skull. Before a scene can be observed “in your head” it has to be broken down into a number of diﬀerent components for processing, and these components then have to be recombined into the meaningful form that we call “an image” . Amongst other things, the scene is broken down into its diﬀerent colours – red, green and blue – in a way that’s analogous to the manner in which a television image or magazine photograph is broken down into tiny dots of primary colors (which are too small to be noticed individually when we look at them, but which when seen collectively give the impression of a continuous full-colour image). However, unlike TV and magazine images, the image that we see with our eyes is broken down not only into separate color components but into other components too. It is, rather incredibly, deconstructed into component parts such as horizontal lines, vertical lines, circles and so on. Each of these component parts is sent to a separate area of the brain for processing, with the diﬀerent components of the scene only merging again when they are uniﬁed into what you perceive as the image.
answer: The scene is broken down into its diﬀerent colors and deconstructed into component parts, and each of these component parts is sent to a separate area of the brain for processing, with the diﬀerent components of the scene only merging again when they are uniﬁed into what you perceive as the image.(52)
question_zh: 重要的是要认识到，大脑并不能简单地将场景投影到头骨内部的电影屏幕上来看待周围的世界。在“在头脑中”观察场景之前，必须将其分解为许多不同的组件进行处理，然后这些组件必须重新组合成有意义的形式，我们称之为“图像”。除此之外，场景被分解成不同的颜色——红色、绿色和蓝色——这类似于电视图像或杂志照片被分解成原色的小点（这些点太小，当我们看它们时无法单独注意到，但当它们集中起来时，给人一种连续的全彩图像的印象）。然而，与电视和杂志图像不同，我们用眼睛看到的图像不仅被分解为单独的颜色成分，而且还被分解为其他成分。令人难以置信的是，它被解构为水平线、垂直线、圆圈等组成部分。这些组成部分中的每一个都被发送到大脑的一个单独区域进行处理，场景的不同组成部分只有在统一成你所感知的图像时才会再次合并。
answer_zh: 场景被分解成不同的颜色并解构为各个组成部分，每个组成部分都被发送到大脑的一个单独区域进行处理，场景的不同组成部分只有在统一成你所感知的图像时才会再次合并。（52）

question: An international team of scientists is set to go to the Arctic to investigate the Greenland shark longevity mystery. The shark is known to be the longest liveing vertebrate animal on the planet Earth. One of the members is Dr. Holy Shiels, a physiologist and senior lecturer in the Faculty of Life Sciences at the University of Manchester. She will be the only British scientist in the team to study the Greenland shark, which is believed to be the vertebrate animal and mammal with the longest-living. The shark is reported to have lived for more than 200 years, and possibly close to or more than 400 years. The shark is both a hunter and a scavenger, which feeds on seals and other animals including polar bears and whales. It is also known as one of the largest sharks, reaching ﬁve and a half meters (18 feet), very close to the size of a great white. The research team is commissioned by the Greenland government and will conduct the research on board the multi-purpose research vessel Sanna, operated by the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources. A Greenland shark is estimated to be able to live for 400 years according to Science Magazine. Professor Shiels expects to gather suﬃcient data on the Greenland shark, a top predator in the Arctic sea. She wanted to ﬁnd a clue to how Greenland shark is able to survive in the deep sea of the Arctic Sea, by examining how its heart and circulation work in its normal habitat, as she specializes in cardiovascular function. "Greenland sharks are classiﬁed as data deﬁcient, " Shiels said. "This means that we don 't know enough to put measures in place to protect them from over-ﬁshing, pollution or climate change. "
answer: An international team of scientists is set to go to the Arctic to investigate the Greenland shark longevity mystery, and one of the members, Professor Shiels, wanted to ﬁnd a clue to how Greenland shark is able to survive in the deep sea of the Arctic sea, by examining how its heart and circulation work in its normal habitat.
question_zh: 一个国际科学家小组将前往北极调查格陵兰鲨鱼的长寿之谜。众所周知，鲨鱼是地球上最长寿的脊椎动物。其中一位成员是Holy Shiels博士，他是曼彻斯特大学生命科学学院的生理学家和高级讲师。她将是研究格陵兰鲨鱼的团队中唯一的英国科学家，格陵兰鲨鱼被认为是最长寿的脊椎动物和哺乳动物。据报道，这条鲨鱼的寿命已超过 200 岁，甚至可能接近或超过 400 岁。鲨鱼既是猎人又是食腐动物，以海豹和其他动物（包括北极熊和鲸鱼）为食。它也被称为最大的鲨鱼之一，长达五米半（18 英尺），非常接近大白鲨的大小。该研究小组受格陵兰政府委托，将在格陵兰自然资源研究所运营的多功能研究船“Sanna”上进行研究。据《科学》杂志报道，格陵兰鲨的寿命估计为 400 年。希尔斯教授希望收集有关北冰洋顶级掠食者格陵兰鲨的足够数据。她专门研究心血管功能，希望通过检查格陵兰鲨在正常栖息地的心脏和血液循环如何工作，找到格陵兰鲨如何在北冰洋深海生存的线索。 “格陵兰鲨鱼被归类为数据缺乏，”希尔斯说。 “这意味着我们了解不够，无法采取措施保护它们免受过度捕捞、污染或气候变化的影响。”
answer_zh: 一个国际科学家小组将前往北极调查格陵兰鲨鱼的长寿之谜，其中一名成员希尔斯教授希望通过检查格陵兰鲨鱼的心脏和循环在其正常栖息地中的运作情况，找到格陵兰鲨鱼如何能够在北冰洋深海生存的线索。

question: subject. When the principal traveled to New Zealand, 第三段 ，Take history as a negative example. There are some problems when it comes to practices. It sometimes combined with art or

Disabled people were among the early adopters of personal computers. They were quick to appreciate that word processing programs and printers gave them freedom from dependence on others to read and write for them. Some of these disabled early adopters became very knowledgeable about what could be achieved and used their knowledge to become independent students at a high level. They also gained the conﬁdence to ask that providers of education make adjustments so that disabled students could make better use of course software and the web, rather than just word processing. For some disability groups, information in electronic format (whether computer-based or web-based) can be more accessible than printed information. For example, people who have limited mobility or limited manual skills can ﬁnd it diﬃcult to obtain or hold printed material; visually impaired people can ﬁnd it diﬃcult or impossible to read print, but both these groups can be enabled to use a computer and, therefore, access the information electronically. Online communication can enable disabled students to communicate with their peers on an equal basis. For example, a deaf student or a student with Asperger 's syndrome may ﬁnd it diﬃcult to interact in a face- to-face tutorial but may have less diﬃculty interacting when using a text conferencing system in which everyone types and reads text. In addition, people’s disabilities are not necessarily visible in online communication systems; so disabled people do not have to declare their disability and are not perceived as being diﬀerent.
answer: Disabled people are among the early adopters of personal computers, become knowledgeable and gain conﬁdence, and for some disability groups, information in electronic format can be more accessible than printed information, and online communication can enable disabled students to communicate with their peers on an equal basis. (Word count: 47)
question_zh: 残疾人是个人电脑的早期采用者之一。他们很快意识到文字处理程序和打印机使他们摆脱了依赖他人为他们阅读和写作的自由。这些残疾的早期采用者中的一些人非常了解可以实现的目标，并利用他们的知识成为高水平的独立学生。他们也有信心要求教育机构做出调整，以便残疾学生能够更好地使用课程软件和网络，而不仅仅是文字处理。对于某些残疾人群体来说，电子格式的信息（无论是基于计算机的还是基于网络的）比印刷信息更容易获取。例如，行动不便或手工技能有限的人可能会发现很难获取或持有印刷材料；视障人士可能会发现阅读印刷品很困难或不可能，但这两个群体都可以使用计算机，从而以电子方式访问信息。在线交流可以使残疾学生能够与同龄人平等交流。例如，聋哑学生或患有阿斯伯格综合症的学生可能会发现在面对面的辅导中互动很困难，但在使用每个人都键入和阅读文本的文本会议系统时，互动的难度可能会较小。此外，人们的残疾不一定在在线通信系统中可见；因此，残疾人不必声明自己的残疾，也不会被视为与众不同。
answer_zh: 残疾人是个人电脑的早期采用者之一，他们变得知识渊博并获得信心，对于某些残疾人群体来说，电子格式的信息比印刷信息更容易获取，而在线交流可以使残疾学生能够在平等的基础上与同龄人交流。 （字数：47）
