answer: Autism is a mental disorder, and no one knows with certainty what caused autism prevalence to rise so precipitously, however, there is a growing awareness among scholars that focusing on individual risk factors and social and institutional processes is suﬃcient to explain this, and although the importance has not been systematically assessed, the literature provides substantial motivation for exploring how these factors to shape the likelihood of an autism diagnosis. (Word count: 70)
question_zh: 自闭症是一种以沟通、社交和重复行为障碍为特征的疾病。过去 40 年来，据测得的自闭症患病率大约增加了 10 倍。尽管在了解与风险增加和患病率上升相关的一些因素方面已经取得了进展，但没有人确切地知道是什么导致了自闭症或导致自闭症患病率急剧上升。然而，学者们越来越认识到，仅仅关注个人风险因素（例如接触有毒物质、产前并发症或父母教育）不足以解释为什么自闭症患病率增长如此惊人。社会和制度进程可能发挥重要作用。例如，诊断标准的变化和专用于自闭症诊断的资源的涌入可能对于理解患病率上升的原因至关重要。自闭症和各种类似疾病的增加与意识和社会影响力的提高有关，这些疾病的社会过程模仿了传染病的影响。研究探讨了诊断标准和诊断替代的变化对自闭症患病率上升的影响，但制度因素、诊断资源和提高认识的重要性尚未得到系统评估。然而，关于健康和不平等的社会学文献为探索个人和社区层面的影响如何影响自闭症诊断的可能性提供了实质性的动力。
answer_zh: 自闭症是一种精神障碍，没有人确切地知道是什么导致自闭症患病率如此急剧上升，然而，学者们越来越意识到，关注个人风险因素以及社会和制度过程足以解释这一点，尽管其重要性尚未得到系统评估，但文献为探索这些因素如何影响自闭症诊断的可能性提供了实质性动力。 （字数：70）

question: Scientists believe they may have found a way to prevent complications that can arise following cataract surgery, the world 's leading cause of blindness. Detailing why complications can occur after surgery, researchers from the University of East Anglia (UEA) explained that while cataract surgery works well to restore vision, a few natural lens cells always remain after the procedure. Over time, the eye 's wound-healing response leads these cells to spread across the underside of the artiﬁcial lens, which interferes with vision, causing what 's known as 'posterior capsule opaciﬁcation ' or secondary cataracts. UEA 's School of Biological Sciences academic, Dr. Michael Wormstone, who led the study, said: "Secondary visual loss responds well to treatment with laser surgery. But as life expectancy increases, the problems of cataracts and posterior capsule opaciﬁcation will become even greater in terms of both patient well-being and economic burden. It 's essential that we ﬁnd better ways to manage the condition in the future. " As a result, researchers are designing new artiﬁcial lenses that can be placed into a capsular bag that stays open, instead of shrink-wrapping closed, which currently occurs. It is believed that, through the new approach, ﬂuid in the eye can ﬂow around the artiﬁcial lens, therefore diluting and washing away the cell-signaling molecules that encourage cell re-growth.
answer: Scientists believe they may have found a way to prevent complications that can arise following cataract surgery, the world’s leading cause of blindness, and since a few natural lens cells always remain after the cataract surgery, secondary cataract will be caused over time, which can cause problems in terms of both patient well-being and economic burden, so researchers are designing new artiﬁcial lenses for ﬂuid in the eye to ﬂow around them.
question_zh: 科学家相信，他们可能已经找到了一种方法来预防白内障手术后可能出现的并发症，白内障是世界上导致失明的主要原因。东安格利亚大学 (UEA) 的研究人员详细解释了手术后出现并发症的原因，他们解释说，虽然白内障手术可以很好地恢复视力，但手术后总会残留一些天然晶状体细胞。随着时间的推移，眼睛的伤口愈合反应会导致这些细胞扩散到人工晶状体的下侧，从而干扰视力，导致所谓的“后囊混浊”或继发性白内障。主持这项研究的东安格利亚大学生物科学学院学者 Michael Wormstone 博士表示：“继发性视力丧失对激光手术的治疗反应良好。但随着预期寿命的延长，白内障和后囊混浊问题在患者健康和经济负担方面将变得更加严重。我们必须找到更好的方法来管理未来的病情。”因此，研究人员正在设计新的人造晶状体，可以放入保持打开状态的囊袋中，而不是目前发生的收缩包装封闭。人们相信，通过这种新方法，眼睛中的液体可以在人造晶状体周围流动，从而稀释并冲走促进细胞重新生长的细胞信号分子。
answer_zh: 科学家们相信，他们可能已经找到了一种方法来预防白内障手术后可能出现的并发症，白内障手术是世界上导致失明的主要原因，而且由于白内障手术后总会残留一些天然晶状体细胞，随着时间的推移会引起继发性白内障，这可能会导致患者的健康和经济负担方面的问题，因此研究人员正在设计新的人造晶状体，让眼睛中的液体在它们周围流动。

question: Life expectancies have been rising by up to three months a year since 1840, and there is no sign of that ﬂattening. Lynda Gratton and Andrew Scott draw on a 2009 study to show that if the trend continues, more than half the babies born in wealthier countries since 2000 may reach their 100th birthdays. With a few simple, devastating strokes, Gratton and Scott show that under the current system ,it is almost certain you won 't be able to save enough to fund several decades of decent retirement. For example, if your life expectancy is 100, you want a pension that is 50 percent of your ﬁnal salary, and you save 10 percent of your earnings each year, they calculate that you won 't be able to retire till your 80s. People with 100-year life expediencies must recognize they are in for the long haul, and make an early start arranging their lives accordingly. But how to go about this? Gratton and Scott advance the idea of a multistage life, with repeated changes of direction and attention. Material and intangible assets will need upkeep, renewal or replacement. Skills will need updating, augmenting or discarding, as will networks of friends and acquaintances. Earning will be interspersed with learning or self-reﬂection. As the authors warn, recreation will have to become re-creation.
answer: Since life expectancies have been rising since 1840, it is almost certain you won’t be able to save enough to fund several decades of decent retirement, so two researchers advance the idea of a multistage life with repeated changes of direction and attention, of which aspects include material and intangible assets, skills, networks of friends and acquaintances, and earning, and recreation will have to become re-creation. (Word count: 68)
question_zh: 自 1840 年以来，预期寿命每年增加三个月，而且没有任何趋平的迹象。琳达·格拉顿 (Lynda Gratton) 和安德鲁·斯科特 (Andrew Scott) 根据 2009 年的一项研究表明，如果这一趋势持续下去，自 2000 年以来在富裕国家出生的婴儿中，一半以上可能会活到 100 岁生日。格拉顿和斯科特用一些简单而毁灭性的笔触表明，在现行制度下，几乎可以肯定你将无法储蓄足够的钱来维持几十年的体面退休生活。例如，如果你的预期寿命是100岁，你想要养老金是你最终工资的50%，你每年将收入的10%存起来，他们计算出你要到80岁才能退休。拥有100年寿命的人必须认识到自己的人生是长远的，并尽早开始相应地安排自己的生活。但这该怎么办呢？格拉顿和斯科特提出了多阶段生活的理念，不断改变方向和注意力。物质和无形资产需要维护、更新或更换。技能需要更新、增强或丢弃，朋友和熟人的网络也需要更新、增强或丢弃。赚钱将伴随着学习或自我反思。正如作者警告的那样，娱乐必须成为再创造。
answer_zh: 自1840年以来，预期寿命一直在增长，几乎可以肯定的是，你将无法攒下足够的钱来维持几十年的体面退休生活，因此两位研究人员提出了多阶段生活的想法，不断改变方向和注意力，其中包括物质和无形资产、技能、朋友和熟人网络以及收入和娱乐必须成为再创造。 （字数：68）

question: Water is at the core of sustainable development. Water resources, and the range of services they provide, underpin poverty reduction, economic growth and environmental sustainability. From food and energy security to human and environmental health, water contributes to improvements in social well- being and inclusive growth, aﬀecting the livelihoods of billions. In a sustainable world that is achievable in the near future, water and related resources are managed in support of human well-being and ecosystem integrity in a robust economy. Suﬃcient and safe water is made available to meet every person 's basic needs, with healthy lifestyles and behaviors easily upheld through reliable and aﬀordable water supply and sanitation services, in turn , supported by equitably extended and eﬃciently managed infrastructure. Water resources management, infrastructure and service delivery are sustainably ﬁnanced. Water is duly valued in all its forms, with wastewater treated as a resource that avails energy, nutrients and freshwater for reuse. Human settlements develop in harmony with the natural water cycle and the ecosystems that support it, with measures in place that reduce vulnerability and improve resilience to water-related disasters. Integrated approaches to water resources development, management and use and to human rights are the norm. Water is governed in a participatory way that draws on the full potential of women and men as professionals and citizens, guided by a number of able and knowledgeable organizations, within a just and transparent institutional framework.
answer: Water is at the core of sustainable development, therefore water resources management, infrastructure and service delivery are sustainably ﬁnanced so that water and related resources are managed in support of human well-being and ecosystem integrity in a sustainable world, and water is duly valued in all its forms, so it is governed and guided within a just and transparent institutional framework.
question_zh: 水是可持续发展的核心。水资源及其提供的一系列服务是减贫、经济增长和环境可持续性的基础。从粮食和能源安全到人类和环境健康，水有助于改善社会福祉和包容性增长，影响着数十亿人的生计。在不久的将来可以实现的可持续发展世界中，对水和相关资源的管理是为了在强劲的经济中支持人类福祉和生态系统的完整性。充足和安全的水可以满足每个人的基本需求，通过可靠和负担得起的供水和卫生服务，可以轻松维护健康的生活方式和行为，反过来，又得到公平扩展和有效管理的基础设施的支持。水资源管理、基础设施和服务提供得到可持续的资助。各种形式的水都受到应有的重视，废水被视为一种资源，可利用能源、营养物和淡水进行再利用。人类住区与自然水循环和支持自然水循环的生态系统和谐发展，并采取措施减少脆弱性并提高对与水有关的灾害的抵御能力。水资源开发、管理和使用以及人权的综合方法已成为常态。水资源以参与性方式进行管理，在公正和透明的体制框架内，在许多有能力和知识渊博的组织的指导下，充分发挥女性和男性作为专业人士和公民的潜力。
answer_zh: 水是可持续发展的核心，因此水资源管理、基础设施和服务提供需要可持续的资金支持，以便对水及相关资源进行管理，以支持可持续世界中的人类福祉和生态系统完整性，并且各种形式的水都得到应有的重视，因此在公正和透明的制度框架内对其进行治理和指导。

question: When Christopher Columbus arrived at Hispaniola during his ﬁrst transatlantic voyage in the year A.D. 1492, the island had already been settled by Native Americans for about 5,000 years. The occupants in Columbus 's time were a group of Arawak Indians called Tainos who lived by farming, were organized into ﬁve chiefdoms, and numbered around half a million (the estimates range from 100,000 to 2000,000). Columbus initially found them peaceful and friendly, until he and his Spaniards began mistreating them. Unfortunately for the Tainos, they had gold, which the Spanish coveted but didn 't want to go to the work of mining themselves. Hence the conquerors divided up the island and its Indian population among individual Spaniards, who put the Indians to work as virtual Slaves, accidentally infected them with Eurasian diseases, and murdered them. By the year 1519, 27 years after Columbus's arrival, that original population of half a million had been reduced to about 11,000, most of whom died that year of smallpox to bring the population down to 3,000.
answer: When Columbus arrived at Hispaniola, it was occupied by Tainos, and Columbus and his Spaniards began to divide up the island and put the Indians to work as virtual slaves since they did not want to go to the work of mining of the gold themselves, but Indian population died out within a few decades due to diseases and smallpox, which forced the Spaniards to look elsewhere for slave laborers.
question_zh: 当克里斯托弗·哥伦布 (Christopher Columbus) 于公元 1492 年第一次跨大西洋航行到达伊斯帕尼奥拉岛时，美洲原住民已经在该岛定居了大约 5,000 年。哥伦布时代的居住者是一群被称为泰诺人的阿拉瓦克印第安人，他们以农业为生，分为五个酋长领地，人数约为 50 万（估计范围从 10 万到 200 万）。哥伦布最初发现他们和平而友好，直到他和他的西班牙人开始虐待他们。不幸的是，对于泰诺人来说，他们拥有黄金，西班牙人对此垂涎欲滴，但又不想自己去采矿。因此，征服者将岛屿及其印第安人分配给了西班牙人，西班牙人让印第安人充当虚拟奴隶，无意中让他们感染了欧亚疾病，然后谋杀了他们。到了 1519 年，即哥伦布抵达 27 年后，原来的 50 万人口已减少到约 11,000 人，其中大多数人在那一年死于天花，使人口减少到 3,000 人。
answer_zh: 当哥伦布抵达伊斯帕尼奥拉岛时，这里已被泰诺人占领，哥伦布和他的西班牙人开始瓜分岛屿，并让印第安人充当虚拟奴隶，因为他们不想自己去开采黄金，但印第安人在几十年内就因疾病和天花而灭绝，这迫使西班牙人到别处寻找奴隶劳工。

question: According to Dr. Ron Fessenden, M.D., M.P.H. the average American consumes more than 150 pounds of reﬁned sugar, plus an additional 62 pounds of high fructose corn syrup every year. In comparison, we consume only around 1.3 pounds of honey per year on average in the U.S. According to new research, if you can switch out your intake of reﬁned sugar and use pure raw honey instead, the health beneﬁts can be enormous. What is raw honey? It 's a pure, unﬁltered and unpasteurized sweetener made by bees from the nectar of ﬂowers. Most of the honey consumed today is processed honey that 's been heated and ﬁltered since it was gathered from the hive. Unlike processed honey, raw honey does not get robbed of its incredible nutritional value and health powers. It can help with everything from low energy to sleep problems to seasonal allergies. Switching to raw honey may even help weight-loss eﬀorts when compared to diets containing sugar or high fructose corn syrup. I 'm excited to tell you more about one of my all-time favorite natural sweeteners today.
answer: According to new research, if you can switch out your intake of reﬁned sugar and use pure raw honey instead, the health beneﬁts can be enormous, and unlike processed honey, raw honey is a pure, unﬁltered and unpasteurized sweetener made by bees and does not get robbed of its incredible nutritional value and health power, which can help with low energy, sleep problems, seasonal allergies and even weight-loss.
question_zh: 根据 Ron Fessenden 博士（医学博士、公共卫生硕士）的说法美国人平均每年消耗超过 150 磅精制糖，另外还要消耗 62 磅高果糖玉米糖浆。相比之下，在美国，我们每年平均仅消耗约 1.3 磅蜂蜜。根据最新研究，如果您可以减少精制糖的摄入量，而使用纯原蜂蜜，那么对健康的好处是巨大的。什么是原蜜？它是一种纯净、未经过滤和未经高温消毒的甜味剂，由蜜蜂从花蜜中提取而成。今天消耗的大部分蜂蜜都是加工过的蜂蜜，从蜂巢中采集后就经过加热和过滤。与加工蜂蜜不同，生蜂蜜不会失去其令人难以置信的营养价值和健康功效。它可以帮助解决从精力不足、睡眠问题到季节性过敏等各种问题。与含糖或高果糖玉米糖浆的饮食相比，改用生蜂蜜甚至可能有助于减肥。今天我很高兴向您介绍我一直以来最喜欢的天然甜味剂之一。
answer_zh: 根据新的研究，如果你可以减少精制糖的摄入量，改用纯生蜂蜜，那么对健康的好处是巨大的，与加工蜂蜜不同，生蜂蜜是一种由蜜蜂制成的纯净、未经过滤和未经高温消毒的甜味剂，不会失去其令人难以置信的营养价值和健康功效，可以帮助解决能量低下、睡眠问题、季节性过敏甚至减肥的问题。

question: In 1815, on the island of Sumbawa in Indonesia, a handsome and long quiescent mountain named Tambora exploded spectacularly, killing a hundred thousand people with its blast and associated tsunamis. No one living now has ever seen such fury. Tambora was far bigger than anything any living human has experienced. It was the biggest volcanic explosion in ten thousand years 150 times the size of Mount St Helens, equivalent to sixty thousand Hiroshima-sized atom bombs. The news didn 't travel terribly fast in those days. In London, The Times ran a small story actually a letter from a merchant - seven months after the event. But by this time Tambora 's eﬀects were already being felt. Two hundred and forty cubic kilometers of smoky ash, dust and grit had diﬀused through the atmosphere, obscuring the Sun 's rays and causing the Earth to cool. Sunsets were unusually but blearily colorful, an eﬀect memorably captured by the artist. J. M. W. Turner, could not have been happier, but mostly the world existed under an oppressive, dusky pall. It was this deathly dimness that inspired Bryon to write the lines quoted above. Spring never came and summer never warmed: 1816 became known as the year without summer. Crops everywhere failed to grow. In Ireland, a famine and associated typhoid epidemic killed sixty-ﬁve thousand people. In New England, the year became popularly known as Eighteen Hundred and Froze to Death. Morning frosts continued until June and almost no planted seed would grow. Short of fodder, livestock died or had to be prematurely slaughtered. In every way it was a dreadful year - almost certainly the worst tor tanners in modern times. Yet globally the temperature fell by less than 1 degree Celsius. The Earth 's natural thermostat, as scientists would learn, is an exceedingly delicate instrument.
answer: In 1815, a mountain called Tambora in Indonesia exploded, which was bigger than anything any living human has experienced, and seven months after the event, The Times ran a small story about it, but by this time, Tambora’s eﬀects have been felt, including smoky ash diﬀusing through the atmosphere, summer being never warmed, no crops and plants growing, epidemic killing people and livestock, and global temperature falling by less than 1 degree Celsius. (Word count: 75)
question_zh: 1815 年，在印度尼西亚的松巴哇岛上，一座名叫坦博拉 (Tambora) 的美丽而漫长的静止山发生了壮观的爆炸，爆炸和相关的海啸导致十万人死亡。现在活着的人还没有见过这样的愤怒。坦博拉比任何活着的人类经历过的任何事情都要大得多。这是一万年来最大的火山爆发，其体积是圣海伦斯火山的150倍，相当于六万颗广岛大小的原子弹。那个时候消息传播得并不快。在伦敦，《泰晤士报》刊登了一篇小故事，实际上是一封来自一位商人的信——事件发生七个月后。但此时坦博拉的影响已经显现。两百四十立方公里的烟灰、灰尘和沙粒扩散到大气中，遮挡了太阳光线，导致地球变冷。日落异常但色彩斑斓，艺术家捕捉到了令人难忘的效果。 J. M. W. 特纳（J. M. W. Turner）真是高兴极了，但世界大多都笼罩在压抑的、昏暗的阴影之下。正是这种死一般的昏暗激发了布莱恩写下上面引用的诗句。春天从未到来，夏天也从未变暖：1816 年被称为“无夏之年”。各地庄稼都无法生长。在爱尔兰，一场饥荒和相关的伤寒疫情导致六万五千人死亡。在新英格兰，这一年被俗称为“一千八百”和“冻死”。晨霜一直持续到六月，几乎没有播种的种子生长。由于缺乏饲料，牲畜死亡或不得不过早宰杀。从各方面来看，这都是可怕的一年——几乎可以肯定，这是现代最糟糕的托尔制革商。然而全球气温下降了不到1摄氏度。正如科学家所知，地球的天然恒温器是一种极其精密的仪器。
answer_zh: 1815年，印度尼西亚一座名叫坦博拉的山发生了爆炸，其规模比任何活着的人类经历过的任何事情都要大，事件发生七个月后，《泰晤士报》刊登了一篇有关此事的小报道，但此时，人们已经感受到了坦博拉山的影响，包括烟尘在大气中扩散，夏季从未变暖，农作物和植物无法生长，流行病导致人和牲畜死亡，全球气温下降不到1摄氏度。 （字数：75）

question: What do great managers actually do? there is one quality that sets truly great managers apart from the rest: They discover what is unique about each person and then capitalize on it. Great managers know and value the unique abilities and even the eccentricities of their employees, and they learn how best to integrate them into a coordinated plan of attack. First, identifying and capitalizing on each person 's uniqueness saves time Second, capitalizing on uniqueness makes each person more accountable. Third, capitalizing on what is unique about each person builds a stronger sense of team.
answer: Great managers discover what is the unique about each person and then capitalize on it, and the beneﬁts include saving time, making each person more accountable, and building a stronger sense of team. (Word count: 33)
question_zh: 伟大的管理者实际上做了什么？真正伟大的管理者有一种与众不同的品质：他们发现每个人的独特之处，然后加以利用。优秀的管理者了解并重视员工的独特能力甚至怪癖，并且他们学习如何最好地将它们整合到协调一致的攻击计划中。首先，识别并利用每个人的独特性可以节省时间。其次，利用独特性可以让每个人更有责任感。第三，利用每个人的独特之处可以建立更强的团队意识。
answer_zh: 优秀的管理者会发现每个人的独特之处，然后加以利用，其好处包括节省时间、让每个人更有责任感以及建立更强的团队意识。 （字数：33）

question: American English is, without doubt, the most inﬂuential and powerful variety of English in the world today. There are many reasons for this. First, the United States is, at present, the most powerful nation on earth and such power always brings with it inﬂuence. Indeed, the distinction between a dialect and a language has frequently been made by reference to power. As has been said, A language is a dialect of an army. Second, America 's political inﬂuence is extended through American popular culture, in particular through the international reach of American ﬁlms (movies, of course) and music. As Kahane has pointed out, The internationally dominant position of American culture results in a forceful expansion of its language.... the expansion of language contributes... to the prestige of the culture behind it. Third, the international prominence of American English is closely associated with the extraordinarily quick development of communications technology. Microsoft is owned by an American, Bill Gates. This means a computer 's default setting for language is American English, although of course this can be changed to suit one 's own circumstances. In short, the increased inﬂuence of American English is caused by political power and the resultant diﬀusion of American culture and media, technological advances and the rapid development of communications technology.
answer: While American English is a dialect with an army because the United States is the most powerful nation on the earth and such power brings with it inﬂuence, America 's political inﬂuence is extended through American popular culture, which also results in an expansion of its language, and the international prominence of American English is associated with the quick development of communications technology, which suggests American English is the most inﬂuential and powerful variety of English.
question_zh: 毫无疑问，美式英语是当今世界上最具影响力和影响力的英语变体。造成这种情况的原因有很多。首先，美国是目前世界上最强大的国家，这种实力总是会带来影响力。事实上，方言和语言之间的区别经常是通过权力来区分的。正如所说，语言是军队的方言。其次，美国的政治影响力是通过美国流行文化，特别是通过美国电影（当然是电影）和音乐的国际影响力来扩展的。正如卡哈恩所指出的，美国文化的国际主导地位导致其语言的有力扩张……语言的扩张有助于……其背后的文化的威望。第三，美式英语的国际影响力与通讯技术的飞速发展密切相关。微软的所有者是美国人比尔·盖茨。这意味着计算机的默认语言设置是美式英语，当然可以根据自己的情况进行更改。简而言之，美式英语影响力的增强是由政治权力以及由此产生的美国文化和媒体的传播、技术进步和通信技术的快速发展造成的。
answer_zh: 美式英语是一种有军队的方言，因为美国是地球上最强大的国家，这种力量带来了影响力，美国的政治影响力是通过美国流行文化延伸的，这也导致了美国语言的扩张，而美式英语的国际地位与通讯技术的快速发展有关，这表明美式英语是最有影响力和最强大的英语变种。

question: Here 's a term you 're going to hear much more often: plug-in vehicle, and the acronym PEV. It 's what you and many other people will drive to work in, ten years and more from now. At that time, before you drive oﬀ in the morning you will ﬁrst unplug your car - your plug-in vehicle. Its big onboard batteries will have been fully charged overnight, with enough power for you to drive 50-100 kilometers through city traﬃc. When you arrive at work you 'll plug in your car once again, this time into a socket that allows power to ﬂow from your car 's batteries to the electricity grid. One of the things you did when you bought your car was to sign a contract with your favorite electricity supplier, allowing them to draw a limited amount of power from your car 's batteries should they need to, perhaps because of a blackout, or very high wholesale spot power prices. The price you get for the power the distributor buys from your car would not only be most attractive to you, it would be a good deal for them too, their alternative being very expensive power from peaking stations. If, driving home or for some other reason your batteries looked like running ﬂat, a relatively small, but quiet and eﬃcient engine running on petrol, diesel or compressed natural gas, even bio-fuel, would automatically cut in, driving a generator that supplied the batteries so you could complete your journey. Concerns over 'peak oil ', increasing greenhouse gas emissions, and the likelihood that by the middle of this century, there could be ﬁve times as many motor vehicles registered worldwide as there are now, mean that the world 's almost total dependence on petroleum-based fuels for transport is, in every sense of the word, unsustainable.
answer: Plug - in vehicles with a small and eﬃcient engine will be what many people drive to work in ten years and more from now , which can be fully charged for you to drive 50 to 100 km , and also , electricity suppliers can draw a limited amount of power from your car 's batteries should they need to , because the world 's almost total dependence on petroleum - based fuels for transport is unsustainable .
question_zh: 这是您经常听到的一个术语：插电式车辆，缩写为 PEV。这就是您和许多其他人在十年甚至更长时间内将驾驶的汽车。那时，在你早上开车​​出发之前，你将首先拔掉你的汽车——你的插电式车辆的插头。它的大型车载电池将在夜间充满电，足够您在城市交通中行驶 50-100 公里。当您到达工作地点时，您将再次插入汽车的电源，这次插入一个允许电力从汽车电池流向电网的插座。当您购买汽车时，您所做的一件事就是与您最喜欢的电力供应商签订合同，允许他们在需要时从您汽车的电池中获取有限的电力，这可能是因为停电或批发现货电价非常高。经销商从你的汽车购买电力的价格不仅对你最有吸引力，而且对他们来说也是一笔划算的交易，他们的替代方案是来自调峰站的非常昂贵的电力。如果开车回家或由于其他原因，你的电池看起来没电了，一个相对较小、但安静、高效的发动机会自动切入，使用汽油、柴油或压缩天然气，甚至生物燃料，驱动发电机为电池供电，这样你就可以完成你的旅程。对“石油峰值”、不断增加的温室气体排放的担忧，以及到本世纪中叶全球登记的机动车辆数量可能是现在的五倍的可能性，意味着世界几乎完全依赖石油基燃料的运输从任何意义上来说都是不可持续的。
answer_zh: 未来十年或更长时间，许多人将驾驶配备小型高效发动机的插电式汽车上班，充满电后可以行驶 50 至 100 公里，而且电力供应商可以根据需要从汽车电池中获取有限的电力，因为世界上几乎完全依赖石油燃料进行运输是不可持续的。

question: As warmer winter temperatures become more common, one way for some animals to adjust is to shift their ranges northward. But a new study of 59 North American bird species indicates that doing so is not easy or quick -- it took about 35 years for many birds to move far enough north for winter temperatures to match where they historically lived. The researchers used 35 years of data from the North American Christmas Bird Count to match winter temperatures to where birds were seen. They tested 59 bird species individually and found that they responded diﬀerently to climate change. When summarized across bird species, there was evidence for a strong delay lasting about 35 years. For example, black vultures have spread northward in the last 35 years and now winter is as far north as Massachusetts, where the minimum winter temperature is similar to what it was in Maryland in 1975. On the other hand, the endangered red-cockaded woodpecker did not alter its range at all despite the warming trend, possibly because its very speciﬁc habitat requirements precluded a range shift. Both of these scenarios could represent problems for birds, La Sorte said. Species that do not track changes in climate may wind up at the limits of their physiological tolerance, or they may lose important habitat qualities, such as favored food types, as those species pass them by. But they also can 't move their ranges too fast if the habitat conditions they depend on also tend to lag behind climate. If warming trends weaken, as they did over the past few years, birds may be able to catch up. But accelerated warming, which is likely as global carbon emissions continue to increase, may put additional strain on birds. The study highlights these challenges and the high potential climate change has for disrupting natural systems. It also underscores the challenges ecologists face in predicting the long-term consequences of climate change for many species simultaneously.
answer: A new study indicates that it took about 35 years for many birds to move far enough north for winter temperatures to match where they historically lived, which could represent problems for birds, because species that do not track changes in climate may wind up at the limits of their physiological tolerance, or lose important habitat qualities, but they also can’t move their ranges too fast. (Word count: 68)
question_zh: 随着冬季气温升高变得越来越普遍，一些动物适应的一种方法是将它们的活动范围向北转移。但一项针对 59 种北美鸟类的新研究表明，做到这一点并不容易或很快——许多鸟类花了大约 35 年的时间才向北迁徙到足够远的地方，使冬季温度能够与它们历史上居住的地方相匹配。研究人员利用 35 年北美圣诞节鸟类统计数据将冬季气温与鸟类出没的地点进行匹配。他们分别测试了 59 种鸟类，发现它们对气候变化的反应不同。当对不同鸟类物种进行总结时，有证据表明明显的延迟持续了大约 35 年。例如，黑秃鹫在过去 35 年里向北扩散，现在的冬季最北可达马萨诸塞州，那里的冬季最低气温与 1975 年马里兰州的气温相似。另一方面，尽管气候变暖，濒临灭绝的红冠啄木鸟并没有改变其分布范围，这可能是因为其非常特殊的栖息地要求阻止了分布范围的变化。拉索尔特说，这两种情况都可能给鸟类带来问题。不跟踪气候变化的物种可能会达到其生理耐受性的极限，或者当这些物种经过它们时，它们可能会失去重要的栖息地品质，例如喜欢的食物类型。但如果它们所依赖的栖息地条件也往往落后于气候，它们也不能太快地移动它们的活动范围。如果变暖趋势减弱，就像过去几年那样，鸟类也许能够迎头赶上。但随着全球碳排放量的持续增加，气候变暖的加速可能会给鸟类带来额外的压力。该研究强调了这些挑战以及气候变化对自然系统破坏的巨大潜力。它还强调了生态学家在同时预测气候变化对许多物种的长期影响时面临的挑战。
answer_zh: 一项新的研究表明，许多鸟类花了大约 35 年的时间才向北迁徙到足够远的地方，以使冬季温度与它们历史上居住的地方相匹配，这可能会给鸟类带来问题，因为不跟踪气候变化的物种可能会达到其生理耐受性的极限，或者失去重要的栖息地质量，但它们也无法太快地移动它们的范围。 （字数：68）

question: What makes teaching online unique is that it uses the Internet, especially the World Wide Web, as the primary means of communication. Thus, when you teach online, you don 't have to be someplace to teach. You don 't have to lug your briefcase full of papers or your laptop to a classroom, stand at a lectern, scribble on a chalkboard (or even use your high-tech, interactive classroom "smart " whiteboard), or grade papers in a stuﬀy room while your students take a test. You don 't even have to sit in your oﬃce waiting for students to show up for conferences. You can hold oﬃce hours on weekends or at night after dinner. You can do all this while living in a small town in Wyoming or a big city like Bangkok, even if you 're working for a college whose administrative oﬃces are located in Florida or Dubai. You can attend an important conference in Hawaii on the same day that you teach your class in New Jersey, logging on from your laptop via the local cafe 's wireless hot spot or your hotel rooms' high-speed network. Or you may simply pull out your smartphone to quickly check on the latest postings, emails, or text messages from students, using a mobile app for your course site or to access other resources. Online learning oﬀers more freedom for students as well. They can search online for courses using the internet, scouring their institutions or even the world for programs, classes, and instructors that ﬁt their needs. Having found an appropriate course, they can enroll and register, shop for their books (whether hard copy or e-books), read articles, listen to lectures, submit their homework assignments, confer with their instructors, and access their ﬁnal grades all online. They can assemble in virtual classrooms, joining other students from diverse geographical locales, and forging bonds and friendships not possible in conventional classrooms, which are usually limited to students from a speciﬁc geographical area.
answer: Using the Internet as its primary communication means , online teaching frees teachers from physical classrooms : they don 't have to be in a speciﬁc place to teach , can work from anywhere , attend conferences while teaching classes elsewhere , and stay connected to students remotely via devices , and online learning also gives students freedom , which means they can access ﬁtting courses globally , get materials and ﬁnish tasks online , and connect with diverse global peers .
question_zh: 在线教学的独特之处在于它使用互联网，特别是万维网作为主要的交流手段。因此，当您在线教学时，您不必在某个地方进行教学。当您的学生参加考试时，您不必拖着装满文件的公文包或笔记本电脑到教室，站在讲台前，在黑板上乱涂乱画（甚至使用高科技交互式课堂“智能”白板），也不必在闷热的房间里对试卷进行评分。您甚至不必坐在办公室等待学生参加会议。您可以在周末或晚上晚餐后保留办公时间。即使您所在的大学的行政办公室位于佛罗里达州或迪拜，您也可以在居住在怀俄明州的小镇或曼谷等大城市时完成这一切。您可以在新泽西州授课的同一天参加在夏威夷举行的重要会议，通过当地咖啡馆的无线热点或酒店房间的高速网络从笔记本电脑登录。或者，您可以简单地拿出智能手机来快速查看学生的最新帖子、电子邮件或短信，使用课程网站的移动应用程序或访问其他资源。在线学习也为学生提供了更多的自由。他们可以使用互联网在线搜索课程，在他们的机构甚至全世界寻找适合他们需求的项目、课程和讲师。找到合适的课程后，他们可以报名和注册、购买书籍（无论是纸质书还是电子书）、阅读文章、听讲座、提交作业、与导师讨论以及在线获取最终成绩。他们可以在虚拟教室中聚集，加入来自不同地理区域的其他学生，并建立传统教室中不可能的纽带和友谊，因为传统教室通常仅限于来自特定地理区域的学生。
answer_zh: 利用互联网作为主要的沟通手段，在线教学将教师从实体教室中解放出来：他们不必在特定的地点进行教学，可以在任何地方工作，在其他地方上课的同时参加会议，并通过设备与学生保持远程联系，在线学习也给了学生自由，这意味着他们可以在全球范围内访问合适的课程，在线获取材料和完成任务，并与不同的全球同行联系。

question: To understand the ﬁnal reason why the news marketplace of ideas dominated by television is so diﬀerent from the one that emerged in the world dominated by the printing press, it is important to distinguish the quality of vividness experienced by television viewers from the vividness experienced by readers. I believe that the vividness experienced in the reading of words is automatically modulated by the constant activation of the reasoning centers of the brain that are used in the process of co-creating the representation of reality the author has intended. By contrast, the visceral vividness portrayed on television has the capacity to trigger instinctual responses similar to those triggered by reality itself and without being modulated by logic, reason, and reﬂective thought. The simulation of reality accomplished in the television medium is so astonishingly vivid and compelling compared with the representations of reality conveyed by printed words that it signiﬁes much more than an incremental change in the way people consume information. Books also convey compelling and vivid representations of reality, of course. However , the reader actively participates in the conjuring of the reality the book 's author is attempting to depict. Moreover, the parts of the human brain that are central to the reasoning process are continually activated by the very act of reading printed words: Words are composed of abstract symbols and letters that have no intrinsic meaning themselves until they are strung together into recognizable sequences. Television, by contrast, presents to its viewers a much more fully formed representation of reality without requiring the creative collaboration that words have always demanded.
answer: The vividness experienced in the reading is automatically modulated by the constant activation of the reasoning centers of the brain, while the visceral vividness portrayed on television triggers instinctual responses without logical modulation, and also the parts of the human brain that are central to the reasoning process are continually activated by reading, while television presents to its viewers a much more fully formed representation of reality without requiring the creative collaboration.
question_zh: 为了理解电视主导的新闻思想市场与印刷机主导的世界中出现的新闻市场如此不同的最终原因，区分电视观众体验到的生动性和读者体验到的生动性非常重要。我相信，阅读文字时所体验到的生动性是通过大脑推理中心的不断激活而自动调节的，这些推理中心在共同创造作者想要的现实表征的过程中被使用。相比之下，电视上描绘的内心生动有能力触发类似于现实本身触发的本能反应，并且不受逻辑、理性和反思性思维的调节。与印刷文字所传达的现实相比，电视媒体对现实的模拟是如此生动和引人注目，它不仅仅意味着人们消费信息方式的渐进变化。当然，书籍也传达了令人信服且生动的现实表现。然而，读者积极参与对本书作者试图描绘的现实的想象。此外，人类大脑中推理过程的核心部分不断被阅读印刷文字的行为所激活：文字由抽象符号和字母组成，它们本身没有内在意义，直到它们被串成可识别的序列。相比之下，电视向观众呈现了更完整的现实表现，而不需要文字一直要求的创造性合作。
answer_zh: 阅读中体验到的生动性是通过大脑推理中心的不断激活而自动调节的，而电视中描绘的本能生动性则无需逻辑调节即可触发本能反应，而人脑中推理过程的核心部分也通过阅读而不断激活，而电视则向观众呈现了更完整的现实再现，而不需要创造性的协作。

question: Tim Berners-Lee believes the internet can foster human understanding and even world peace. He is the man who has changed the world more than anyone else in the past hundred years. Sir Tim Berners-Lee may be a mild-mannered academic who lives modestly in Boston, but as the inventor of the World Wide Web, he is also a revolutionary. Along with Galileo, William Caxton and Sir Isaac Newton, he is a scientist who has altered the way people think as well as the way they live. Since the web went global 20 years ago, the way we shop, listen to music and communicate has been transformed. There are implications for politics, literature, economics even terrorism because an individual can now have the same access to information as the elite. Society will never be the same. The computer scientist from Oxford, who built his own computer from a television screen and spare parts after he was banned from one of the university computers, is a cultural guru as much as a technological one. It is amazing how far we 've come, he says. But you 're always wondering what 's the next crazy idea, and working to make sure the web stays one web and that the internet stays open. There isn 't much time to sit back and reﬂect. He invented the web, he says, because he was frustrated that he couldn 't ﬁnd all the information he wanted in one place. It was an imaginary concept that he realized.
answer: Tim Bemers-Lee, the inventor of the world wide web, has amazingly altered the way people think and live which is associated with politics, literature, economics even terrorism, but people are always wondering what 's the next crazy idea.(Word count:37)
question_zh: 蒂姆·伯纳斯·李相信互联网可以促进人类理解甚至世界和平。他是近百年来对世界改变最大的人。蒂姆·伯纳斯·李爵士可能是一位举止温和的学者，生活在波士顿，生活简朴，但作为万维网的发明者，他也是一位革命者。他与伽利略、威廉·卡克斯顿和艾萨克·牛顿爵士一样，是一位改变了人们思维方式和生活方式的科学家。自 20 年前网络走向全球以来，我们购物、听音乐和交流的方式已经发生了变化。这对政治、文学、经济甚至恐怖主义都有影响，因为个人现在可以像精英一样获得信息。社会将永远不再一样。这位来自牛津大学的计算机科学家在被禁止使用大学计算机后，用电视屏幕和零部件建造了自己的计算机，他既是一位文化大师，也是一位技术大师。 “我们已经取得了如此大的进步，真是令人惊讶，”他说。但您总是想知道下一个疯狂的想法是什么，并努力确保网络保持同一个网络并且互联网保持开放。没有太多时间坐下来反思。他说，他发明了网络，因为他对无法在一个地方找到他想要的所有信息感到沮丧。这是他意识到的一个想象的概念。
answer_zh: 万维网的发明者蒂姆·贝默斯-李惊人地改变了人们与政治、文学、经济甚至恐怖主义相关的思维和生活方式，但人们总是想知道下一个疯狂的想法是什么。（字数：37）

question: Sanford J. Ungar Athenaeum is a high-tech library, a public forum, a cafe, an art gallery, a radio station—and many other spaces—all in one. You might say it 's the intellectual, cultural, and social crossroads of the campus.
question_zh: Sanford J. Ungar Athenaeum 集高科技图书馆、公共论坛、咖啡馆、艺术画廊、广播电台以及许多其他空间于一体。你可能会说这是校园的知识、文化和社会十字路口。

question: Malaysia is one of the most pleasant, hassle-free countries to visit in Southeast Asia. Aside from its gleaming 21st-century glass towers, it boasts some of the most superb beaches, mountains and national parks in the region. Malaysia is also launching its biggest-ever tourism campaign in an eﬀort to lure 20 million visitors here this year. Tourism is the second- largest source of foreign exchange in Southeast Asian nations apart from exports. Any tourist itinerary would have to begin in the capital, Kuala Lumpur, where you will ﬁnd the Petronas Twin Towers, which once comprised the world 's tallest buildings and now hold the title of second-tallest. Both the 88-story towers soar 1,480 feet high and are connected by a sky bridge on the 41st ﬂoor. The limestone temple Batu Caves, located 9 miles north of the city, has a 328-foot-high ceiling and features ornate Hindu shrines, including a 141-foot-tall gold- painted statue of a Hindu deity. To reach the caves, visitors have to climb a steep ﬂight of 272 steps. In Sabah state on Borneo island not to be confused with Indonesian Borneo you 'll ﬁnd the small mushroom-shaped Sipadan island, oﬀ the coast of Sabah, rated as one of the top ﬁve diving sites in the world. Sipadan is the only oceanic island in Malaysia, rising from a 2,300-foot abyss in the Celebes Sea. You can also climb Mount Kinabalu, the tallest peak in Southeast Asia, visit the Sepilok Orang Utan Sanctuary, go white-water rafting and catch a glimpse of the bizarre Proboscis monkey, a primate found only in Borneo with a huge pendulous nose, a characteristic pot belly and strange honking sounds. While you 're in Malaysia, consider a trip to Malacca. In its heyday, this southern state was a powerful Malay sultanate and a booming trading port in the region. Facing the Straits of Malacca, this historical state is now a place of intriguing Chinese streets, antique shops, old temples and reminders of European colonial powers. Another interesting destination is Penang, known as the Pearl of the Orient. This island oﬀ the northwest coast of Malaysia boasts a rich Chinese cultural heritage, good food and beautiful beaches.
answer: Malaysia, which is one of the most pleasant, hassle-free countries to visit in Southeast Asia with gleaming 21st century glass towers and the most superb beaches, mountains and national parks, is launching its biggest-ever tourism campaign in an eﬀort to lure 20 million visitors this year, and with an itinerary starting from Kuala Lumpur and ending in Malacca, you can enjoy a lot of rich cultural heritage, good food and beautiful beaches.
question_zh: 马来西亚是东南亚最令人愉快、无忧无虑的国家之一。除了闪闪发光的 21 世纪玻璃塔外，它还拥有该地区一些最美丽的海滩、山脉和国家公园。马来西亚今年还推出了有史以来规模最大的旅游活动，力求吸引 2000 万游客。旅游业是东南亚国家除出口外的第二大外汇来源。任何旅游行程都必须从首都吉隆坡开始，在那里您会看到双子塔，它曾经是世界上最高的建筑，现在拥有第二高的称号。两座 88 层的塔楼均高达 1,480 英尺，并通过 41 层的天桥相连。石灰岩寺庙黑风洞 (Batu Caves) 位于城市以北 9 英里处，拥有 328 英尺高的天花板和华丽的印度教神殿，其中包括一座 141 英尺高的印度教神祇的金色雕像。要到达洞穴，游客必须爬 272 级陡峭的台阶。在婆罗洲岛的沙巴州，不要与印度尼西亚婆罗洲混淆，您会发现位于沙巴海岸附近的蘑菇形状的西巴丹小岛，被评为世界五个最佳潜水地点之一。西巴丹岛是马来西亚唯一的海洋岛屿，从西里伯斯海 2,300 英尺深的深渊中拔地而起。您还可以攀登东南亚最高峰基纳巴卢山，参观西必洛红毛猩猩保护区，进行激流漂流，并一睹奇特的长鼻猴的风采，长鼻猴是一种仅在婆罗洲发现的灵长类动物，拥有巨大的下垂鼻子、特有的大肚皮和奇怪的鸣叫声。当您在马来西亚时，请考虑前往马六甲旅行。在其鼎盛时期，这个南部州属是一个强大的马来苏丹国，也是该地区蓬勃发展的贸易港口。面对马六甲海峡，这个历史悠久的国家现在是一个充满迷人的中国街道、古董店、古老寺庙和欧洲殖民列强的地方。另一个有趣的目的地是被誉为东方之珠的槟城。这个位于马来西亚西北海岸的岛屿拥有丰富的中国文化遗产、美味的食物和美丽的海滩。
answer_zh: 马来西亚是东南亚最令人愉快、无忧无虑的国家之一，拥有闪闪发光的21世纪玻璃塔和最美丽的海滩、山脉和国家公园，今年将推出有史以来最大规模的旅游活动，力图吸引2000万游客，从吉隆坡开始到马六甲结束的行程，您可以享受到丰富的文化遗产、美食和美丽的海滩。

question: When the Rosetta Stone was discovered in 1799, the carved characters that covered its surface were quickly copied. Printers ink was applied to the Stone and white paper was laid over it. When the paper was removed, it revealed an exact copy of the text but in reverse. Since then, many copies or facsimiles have been made using a variety of materials. Inevitably, the surface of the Stone accumulated many layers of material left over from these activities, despite attempts to remove any residue. Once on display, the grease from many thousands of human hands eager to touch the Stone added to the problem. An opportunity to investigate and clean the Rosetta Stone arose when this famous object was made the centerpiece of the Cracking Codes exhibition at The British Museum in 1999. When work commenced to remove all but the original, ancient material, the stone was black with white lettering. As treatment progressed, the diﬀerent substances uncovered were analyzed. Grease from human handling, a coating of carnauba wax from the early 1800s and printer ink from 1799 were cleaned away using cotton wool swabs and liniment of soap, white spirit, acetone and puriﬁed water. Finally, white paint in the text, applied in 1981, which had been left in place until now as a protective coating, was removed with cotton swabs and puriﬁed water. A small square at the bottom left corner of the face of the Stone was left untouched to show the darkened wax and the white inﬁll.
answer: Since the Rosetta Stone was discovered in 1799, many copies or facsimiles have been made using a variety of materials, along with many thousands of human hands eager to touch the Stone, causing the surface of the Stone accumulated many layers of materials, and an opportunity for investigation and cleaning the stone arose at the British Museum in 1999, after which all but the origin was removed, and the stone was black with white lettering. (Word count: 75)
question_zh: 1799 年罗塞塔石碑被发现后，其表面的雕刻文字很快就被复制。将打印机墨水涂在石头上，并在上面铺上白纸。当纸被移除时，它显示出文本的精确副本，但相反。从那时起，人们使用各种材料制作了许多副本或传真件。尽管试图清除任何残留物，但石头的表面不可避免地积累了许多层这些活动留下的物质。一旦展出，成千上万渴望触摸这块石头的人手上的油脂加剧了这个问题。 1999 年，当罗塞塔石碑成为大英博物馆“破解密码”展览的核心展品时，研究和清理罗塞塔石碑的机会出现了。当工作开始清除除原始古老材料之外的所有材料时，石头呈黑色，带有白色字体。随着治疗的进展，对发现的不同物质进行了分析。使用脱脂棉签和肥皂搽剂、石油溶剂油、丙酮和纯净水清除人工处理产生的油脂、1800 年代初的巴西棕榈蜡涂层和 1799 年的打印机墨水。最后，用棉签和纯净水将 1981 年涂上的白色油漆（一直作为保护涂层保留在原处）清除掉。石头表面左下角的一个小方块未被触及，以显示深色的蜡和白色的填充物。
answer_zh: 自1799年罗塞塔石碑被发现以来，人们用各种材料制作了许多复制品或复制品，加上成千上万的人手渴望触摸石头，导致石头表面积累了多层材料，1999年大英博物馆出现了对石头进行调查和清理的机会，之后石头除了原点外全部被去除，石头呈黑底白字。 （字数：75）

question: UCLA neurology professor Paul Thompson and his colleagues scanned the brains of 23 sets of identical twins and 23 sets of fraternal twins. Since identical twins share the same genes while fraternal twins share about half their genes, the researchers were able to compare each group to show that myelin integrity was determined genetically in many parts of the brain that are key for intelligence. These include the parietal lobes, which are responsible for spatial reasoning, visual processing and logic, and the corpus callosum, which pulls together information from both sides of the body. The researchers used a faster version of a type of scanner called a HARDI (high-angular resolution diﬀusion imaging) think of an MRI machine on steroids that takes scans of the brain at a much higher resolution than a standard MRI. While an MRI scan shows the volume of diﬀerent tissues in the brain by measuring the amount of water present, HARDI tracks how water diﬀuses through the brain 's white matter a way to measure the quality of its myelin. "HARDI measures water diﬀusion, " said Thompson, who is also a member of the UCLA Laboratory of Neuro-Imaging. "If the water diﬀuses rapidly in a speciﬁc direction, it tells us that the brain has very fast connections. If it diﬀuses more broadly, that 's an indication of slower signaling and lower intelligence. "
answer: Research on twins has shown that myelin integrity was determined genetically in many parts of the brain that are key for intelligence, and the researchers used a faster version of a type of scanner called a HARDI, which tracks how water diﬀuses through the brain’s white matter, a way to measure the quality of its myelin, and if water diﬀuses rapidly, it tells the brain has very fast connections and higher intelligence. (Word count: 74)
question_zh: 加州大学洛杉矶分校神经学教授 Paul Thompson 和他的同事扫描了 23 组同卵双胞胎和 23 组异卵双胞胎的大脑。由于同卵双胞胎共享相同的基因，而异卵双胞胎共享大约一半的基因，因此研究人员能够对每个组进行比较，以表明髓鞘质的完整性是由大脑中许多对智力至关重要的部分决定的。其中包括负责空间推理、视觉处理和逻辑的顶叶，以及汇集身体两侧信息的胼胝体。研究人员使用了一种名为 HARDI（高角分辨率扩散成像）扫描仪的更快版本，它是一种类固醇 MRI 机器，以比标准 MRI 更高的分辨率对大脑进行扫描。 MRI 扫描通过测量存在的水量来显示大脑中不同组织的体积，而哈滴则跟踪水如何在大脑白质中扩散，从而测量其髓磷脂的质量。 “哈滴测量水的扩散，”汤普森说，他也是加州大学洛杉矶分校神经成像实验室的成员。 “如果水在特定方向上快速扩散，则表明大脑的连接速度非常快。如果水扩散得更广泛，则表明信号传导较慢，智力较低。”
answer_zh: 对双胞胎的研究表明，髓鞘质的完整性是由基因决定的，在大脑的许多部位都是智力的关键，研究人员使用了一种名为 HARDI 的扫描仪，它的速度更快，它可以追踪水如何在大脑白质中扩散，这是一种测量髓鞘质质量的方法，如果水扩散得很快，就表明大脑的连接速度非常快，智力也很高。 （字数：74）

title_zh: 图书馆的服务不可练习
question: 务 ，建立database和网站之类的。后面说这个报告光说没用 ，没有实际作用 ，所以相关人员成立小组 ，根据这个报告开始做一些实际上的策略指导工作。

Kids mimic what their parents do — and a new study on TV-viewing habits proves just that. Research published July 15 in Paediatrics shows that the amount of time parents watch TV is connected to how much TV their children watch, even more so than the location of the TV in the home or the family’s rules for television watching. The American Academy of Paediatrics suggests that children and teens should only be allowed to use “high-quality” entertainment media for one to two hours per day. In addition, the house should have “screen-free” zones like the children’s bedroom, where there are no TVs, computer games or video games. The TV should be turned oﬀ during dinner, the academy adds. Each hour of TV viewed by the parents was linked to an additional half-hour of viewing time for children. Children whose parents watched more than the average also watched more compared to kids whose parents stuck to the four hours daily. Parents’ TV time had a stronger association with how much time children watched television compared to house rules on time limits, whether the children had a TV in the bedroom and whether the family was watching together. Parents who restricted television time only were able to cut down viewing times for children who were in the 6 to 11-year-old age group. Adolescents watched about one more hour of TV than their parents thought they did, the results also showed.
answer: The amount of time parents watch TV is connected to how much TV their children watch because kids mimics what their parents do, and the American Academy of Paediatrics suggests that children and teens should only be allowed to use high-quality entertainment media for one to two hours per day and the should have “screen-free”zones, and adolescents watched about one more hour of TV than their parents thought they did. (Word count: 73)
question_zh: 孩子们模仿父母的行为——一项关于电视观看习惯的新研究证明了这一点。 7 月 15 日发表在《儿科》杂志上的研究表明，父母看电视的时间与孩子看电视的时间有关，甚至比电视在家中的位置或家庭看电视的规则更重要。美国儿科学会建议，儿童和青少年每天只能使用“高质量”娱乐媒体一到两个小时。此外，房子应该有“无屏幕”区域，例如儿童卧室，那里没有电视、电脑游戏或视频游戏。该学院补充说，晚餐时应关闭电视。父母每看一个小时的电视，孩子的观看时间就会增加半个小时。与父母每天坚持观看四个小时的孩子相比，父母观看时间超过平均水平的孩子观看的时间也更多。与时间限制、孩子卧室里是否有电视以及家人是否一起看电视的家庭规则相比，父母看电视的时间与孩子看电视的时间有更强的关联。仅限制看电视时间的父母能够减少 6 至 11 岁年龄段儿童的观看时间。研究结果还显示，青少年看电视的时间比父母想象的多了大约一小时。
answer_zh: 父母看电视的时间与孩子看电视的时间有关，因为孩子会模仿父母的行为，美国儿科学会建议，儿童和青少年每天只能使用高质量的娱乐媒体一到两个小时，并且应该设立“无屏幕”区域，青少年看电视的时间比父母想象的多大约一小时。 （字数：73）

question: Compulsory voting is often suggested as a solution to the problem of declining turnout. But how are individuals and countries aﬀected by compulsory voting beyond boosting electoral participation? Shane Singh investigates the social, economic, and political consequences of compelling citizens to vote. There has been a lot of discussion about compulsory voting these days. In the United Kingdom, in particular, as voter turnout rates have declined, many commentators and politicians have begun advocating for mandatory electoral participation. Those in favor of compulsory voting often adduce the importance of participation among all segments of society. Citizens of democracies are forced to do many things in the interest of the public good, they maintain, including serving on juries and educating their children, and full participation serves the country as a whole. Those opposed to compulsory voting often argue that, from a democratic theory perspective, the right to vote implicitly includes a right not to vote. Such a right of abstention, they argue, is more important than any societal good that might accompany high turnout. In fact, opponents of compulsory voting often contend that the country may be better oﬀ if those who are disinclined to vote are not pushed to participate in public aﬀairs. Regardless of whether one of these sets of arguments is more persuasive than the other, compulsory voting is commonly used around the world. Several European democracies mandate voting, as do Australia and most of the countries in Latin America. By evaluating results from these countries, it is possible to assess the mechanics and eﬀects of compulsory voting.
answer: There has been a lot of discussion about compulsory voting these days, and speciﬁcally, those in favor of compulsory voting often adduce the importance of participation among all segments of society but opponents of compulsory voting often contend that the country may be better oﬀ if those who are disinclined to vote are not pushed to participate in public aﬀairs, while compulsory voting is commonly used around the world. (Word count:69)
question_zh: 强制投票经常被建议作为投票率下降问题的解决方案。但是，除了提高选举参与度之外，强制投票对个人和国家有何影响？肖恩·辛格（Shane Singh）调查了强迫公民投票的社会、经济和政治后果。这些天关于强制投票的讨论很多。特别是在英国，随着选民投票率下降，许多评论员和政界人士开始倡导强制性选举参与。那些支持强制投票的人经常强调社会各阶层参与的重要性。他们认为，民主国家的公民被迫为了公共利益而做很多事情，包括担任陪审团成员和教育他们的孩子，而充分参与为整个国家服务。那些反对强制投票的人常常认为，从民主理论的角度来看，投票权隐含着不投票权。他们认为，这种弃权权比高投票率可能带来的任何社会福利都更重要。事实上，强制投票的反对者经常声称，如果不强迫那些不愿投票的人参与公共事务，国家的境况可能会更好。无论这组论点中的一组是否比另一组更有说服力，强制投票在世界各地都普遍使用。一些欧洲民主国家强制投票，澳大利亚和大多数拉丁美洲国家也是如此。通过评估这些国家的结果，可以评估强制投票的机制和效果。
answer_zh: 现在关于强制投票的讨论很多，具体来说，支持强制投票的人经常强调社会各阶层参与的重要性，而反对强制投票的人则经常认为，如果不强迫那些不愿意投票的人参与公共事务，国家可能会变得更好，而强制投票在世界各地都很普遍。 （字数：69）

question: A democratic country should have the right to decide whether to vote or not. It is strange that after decades of crawling up the political backside of the US, Australians don 't have that right. Being ﬁned for not voting reminds me of the old saying "You can lead a horse to water but you cannot make him drink ". The ﬁne is not for failing to vote but for failing to have your name marked oﬀ a list! Forcing people to make a decision just means they'll make the easiest, quickest decision they can, not the best one. You need an informed electorate for compulsory voting to work. However, the reality is that nobody knows anything about the candidates and promotional material is not readily available. I 'd rather 80% of people didn 't vote than have them all just pick the ﬁrst recognizable name on the ballot sheet. Then at least the government is elected by the 20% who care and make informed decisions. Otherwise, it is largely pot chance who gets elected. Furthermore, compulsory voting doesn 't ensure that the entire electorate is engaged in the democratic process. Those who don 't want to vote can simply turn up and get their name marked oﬀ , without even putting pencil to paper. But you 're seriously deluding yourself if you think that this is what all those who don 't care about the government do when they turn up to the polling booth. Voluntary voting at least ensures those who vote are the ones who care enough to do so. Perhaps somebody could enlighten me as to the reason why, to the best of my knowledge, Australia is the only 'democracy' that has compulsory voting. It is certainly not compulsory in the USA, England, Canada, New Zealand, Philippines or any other European or Asian democracy that I am aware of. Compulsory voting is, however, mandatory in most communist regimes.
answer: A democratic country should have the right to decide whether to vote or not, but Australians don 't have that right, and the reality is that nobody knows anything about the candidates and promotional material is not readily available, and compulsory voting doesn 't ensure that the entire electorate is engaged in the democratic process, and voluntary voting at least ensures those who vote are the ones that care enough to do so. (71 words)
question_zh: 民主国家应该有权利决定是否投票。奇怪的是，在美国政治背后爬了几十年之后，澳大利亚人却没有这个权利。因不投票而被罚款让我想起了一句老话“你可以牵马到水边，但你不能强迫他喝水”。罚款不是因为没有投票，而是因为没有将你的名字从名单上划掉！强迫人们做出决定只是意味着他们会做出最简单、最快的决定，而不是最好的决定。您需要知情的选民才能让强制投票发挥作用。然而，现实情况是，没有人对候选人有任何了解，宣传材料也不容易获得。我宁愿 80% 的人不投票，也不愿让他们都选择选票上第一个可识别的名字。那么至少政府是由关心并做出明智决定的 20% 的人选出的。否则，当选的机会很大。此外，强制投票并不能确保所有选民都参与民主进程。那些不想投票的人可以简单地出现并把他们的名字划掉，甚至不需要用铅笔在纸上写下来。但如果你认为所有不关心政府的人来到投票站时都会这么做，那你就严重自欺欺人了。自愿投票至少可以确保投票者是那些足够关心投票的人。也许有人可以启发我，据我所知，为什么澳大利亚是唯一实行强制投票的“民主国家”。据我所知，在美国、英国、加拿大、新西兰、菲律宾或任何其他欧洲或亚洲民主国家，这当然不是强制性的。然而，在大多数共产主义政权中，强制投票是强制性的。
answer_zh: 一个民主国家应该有权决定是否投票，但澳大利亚人没有这个权利，现实是没有人了解候选人，宣传材料也不易获得，强制投票并不能确保全体选民都参与民主进程，而自愿投票至少可以确保投票的是那些足够关心的人。 （71 个字）

question: Skipping breakfast seems a simple way of losing weight or saving time while getting the children ready for school or rushing oﬀ to work. But it can also be a sign of an unhealthy lifestyle with potentially dangerous consequences, including a higher risk of premature death. According to a study, adults and teenagers who miss the ﬁrst meal of the day are less likely to look after their health. They tend to smoke more, drink more alcohol and take less exercise than those who do eat. Those who skip food in the morning are also more likely to be fatter and less well-educated, meaning they ﬁnd it harder to get a job. Researcher Dr. Anna Keski- Rahkonen said that Smoking, infrequent exercise, a low level of education, frequent alcohol use and a high body mass index were all associated with skipping breakfast in adults and adolescents. Our ﬁndings suggest this association exists throughout adulthood. Individuals who skip breakfast may care less about their health than those who eat breakfast. Previously, experts assumed that missing breakfast often called the most important meal of the day was simply the marker of a hectic life or a way to try to lose weight. But Dr. Keski-Rahkonen, who led the study at Helsinki University, said the results revealed starting the day without food suggests an unhealthy lifestyle.
answer: Although skipping breakfast seems a simple way of losing weight and was the marker of a hectic life, a study has revealed that more smoking and drinking, less exercise, being fatter and less educated as well as higher body mass index are all associated to the adults who miss ‘the most important meal of the day’, and this association exists during adulthood. (Word count:62 )
question_zh: 不吃早餐似乎是一种简单的减肥方法，或者可以节省时间，同时让孩子们准备好上学或赶去上班。但这也可能是不健康生活方式的标志，可能会带来潜在的危险后果，包括更高的过早死亡风险。一项研究表明，错过第一顿饭的成年人和青少年不太可能照顾自己的健康。与那些吃东西的人相比，他们往往抽烟更多、喝酒更多、运动更少。那些早上不吃饭的人也更有可能变得更胖并且受教育程度较低，这意味着他们更难找到工作。研究人员 Anna Keski-Rahkonen 博士表示，吸烟、不经常运动、教育水平低、经常饮酒和体重指数高都与成人和青少年不吃早餐有关。我们的研究结果表明这种关联存在于整个成年期。不吃早餐的人可能比吃早餐的人更不关心自己的健康。此前，专家认为，不吃早餐（通常被称为一天中最重要的一餐）只是忙碌生活的标志，或者是尝试减肥的一种方式。但赫尔辛基大学领导这项研究的凯斯基-拉科宁博士表示，结果显示，一天不吃东西表明生活方式不健康。
answer_zh: 尽管不吃早餐似乎是一种简单的减肥方法，也是忙碌生活的标志，但一项研究表明，更多的吸烟和饮酒、更少的运动、更胖、受教育程度更低以及更高的体重指数都与成年人错过“一天中最重要的一餐”有关，而且这种关联在成年期间都存在。 （字数：62）

question: The booksellers of Hookham and Carpenter (hereafter referred to only as Hookham) were located on New Bond Street in London, and their records span the most politically turbulent decade of the eighteenth-century the 1790s. Clients who frequented Hookham were primarily from the aristocratic or gentry classes. In fact, of Hookham 's total buyers, 22% were the aristocracy, and 35% of the aristocracy purchased novels. We can also conﬁdently assume that untitled female customers were of gentry income because their addresses were primarily in London 's fashionable West End. Hookham ledgers not only reveal a dramatic increase in the proportion of female purchasers of novels by comparison to earlier studies of provincial women, but they also reveal a remarkable increase in the proportion of female purchases of novels authored by females. Such a marked increase illustrates that Hookham leisured female customers were able to buy more novels. Furthermore, the fact that these female aristocrats and gentry have accounts under their own name, not their husbands, demonstrates the greater degree of agency and independence that these urban, moneyed women had relative to provincial women. However, because our study does not include an examination of male customers, we are very limited in what claims we can make about whether or not these women behaved according to the cliche that women were the predominant consumers of novels in the eighteenth century. Moreover, while more disposable income and leisure time certainly account for the signiﬁcant increase in female purchases of novels authored by women in the 1790s, this increase also strongly suggests a desire on the part of women readers to engage in this politically charged decade. Thus, novel-reading provided women readers with the means through which they were able to participate in the male-dominated world of politics. The latter part of our paper will more fully explore this hypothesis in the context of certain recent literary scholars' claims that both Gothic and sentimental novels are actively engaged in political debate and discussion.
answer: According to Hookham 's ﬁndings, there is a dramatic increase in the proportion of female purchasers of novels and purchases of novels authored by females, and also, these female aristocrats and gentry have accounts under their own names, and more disposable income and leisure time certainly account for the signiﬁcant increase, thus more female were able to participate in the male-dominated world of politics.
question_zh: Hookham and Carpenter（以下简称 Hookham）书商位于伦敦新邦德街，他们的记录跨越了 1790 年代 18 世纪政治最动荡的十年。经常光顾胡克姆的顾客主要来自贵族或士绅阶层。事实上，在胡克姆的总买家中，22%是贵族，其中35%的贵族购买了小说。我们还可以自信地假设，无头衔的女性顾客具有贵族收入，因为她们的地址主要位于伦敦时尚的西区。胡克姆分类账不仅显示，与早期对省级女性的研究相比，女性小说购买者的比例显着增加，而且还显示，女性购买女性创作的小说的比例显着增加。如此显着的增长表明，胡克姆闲暇的女性顾客能够购买更多的小说。此外，这些女性贵族和绅士的账户都在自己的名下，而不是在她们丈夫的名下，这一事实表明，这些有钱的城市女性相对于外省女性拥有更大程度的能动性和独立性。然而，由于我们的研究不包括对男性顾客的调查，因此我们对这些女性的行为是否符合“女性是十八世纪小说的主要消费者”这一陈词滥调的说法的判断非常有限。此外，虽然更多的可支配收入和闲暇时间肯定是 1790 年代女性购买女性创作的小说显着增加的原因，但这种增长也强烈表明女性读者渴望参与这个充满政治色彩的十年。因此，小说阅读为女性读者提供了参与男性主导的政治世界的手段。我们论文的后半部分将在最近某些文学学者声称哥特小说和感伤小说都积极参与政治辩论和讨论的背景下更全面地探讨这一假设。
answer_zh: 根据胡克汉姆的研究结果，女性购买小说和购买女性作者的小说的比例急剧增加，而且这些女性贵族和绅士拥有自己名下的账户，更多的可支配收入和闲暇时间肯定是这种显着增加的原因，因此更多的女性能够参与男性主导的政治世界。

question: In 2005, Japan had the highest median age of all countries in the world, while Australia 's population was only moderately aged. Some 50 years ago the demographic situation was quite diﬀerent, with the median age of Australia 's population being seven years older than Japan 's. The aging of the population is a major issue for Australian policymakers, particularly in regard to the long-term implications for reduced economic growth and the increasing demand for Age Pensions, and health and aged care services. As the population ages, growth in the number of people of working age will slow, while the proportion of people of retirement age will increase. Sustained population aging also leads to slowing or negative population growth. While declining population growth in developed countries is welcomed by some environmentalists and social scientists, economists tend to agree that population decline brings gloomy economic prospects. In addition to the decrease in the labor supply, the demand side of the economy may be aﬀected by shrinking markets for goods and services. How quickly this occurs depends on the dynamics of fertility, mortality and overseas migration. While a moderate pace of demographic change allows for gradual adjustment of the economy and policies to the changing population demographics, rapid changes are more diﬃcult to manage. As a result, governments and society as a whole may need to take action to address these issues. But how severe is the aging of Australia 's population, relative to other countries?
answer: In 2005 Australia’s population was only moderately aged, but the demographic situation will be quite diﬀerent, which indicates that the aging of the population is a major issue for Australian policymakers in regard to economy and health services, and also sustained population aging leads to slowing or negative population growth that can bring gloomy economic prospects, so governments and society need to take actions to address these issues. (Word count: 70)
question_zh: 2005年，日本的平均年龄是世界上最高的，而澳大利亚的人口年龄适中。大约 50 年前，人口状况已大不相同，澳大利亚人口的中位年龄比日本大 7 岁。人口老龄化是澳大利亚政策制定者面临的一个主要问题，特别是考虑到经济增长放缓以及对养老金、健康和老年护理服务的需求不断增加的长期影响。随着人口老龄化，劳动年龄人口的增长将放缓，而退休年龄人口的比例将增加。持续的人口老龄化也会导致人口增长放缓或负增长。虽然发达国家人口增长下降受到一些环保主义者和社会科学家的欢迎，但经济学家倾向于认为人口下降带来暗淡的经济前景。除了劳动力供应减少之外，经济的需求面也可能受到商品和服务市场萎缩的影响。这种情况发生的速度取决于生育率、死亡率和海外移民的动态。虽然适度的人口变化允许逐步调整经济和政策以适应不断变化的人口结构，但快速的变化更难以管理。因此，政府和整个社会可能需要采取行动来解决这些问题。但相对于其他国家，澳大利亚人口老龄化有多严重？
answer_zh: 2005年澳大利亚人口只是中等老龄化，但人口状况将有很大不同，这表明人口老龄化是澳大利亚政策制定者在经济和医疗卫生服务方面面临的重大问题，而且持续的人口老龄化导致人口增长放缓或负增长，从而带来暗淡的经济前景，因此政府和社会需要采取行动解决这些问题。 （字数：70）

question: A company in the USA is paying its employees to sleep more. Staﬀ at the insurance company Aetna will get $300 a year added to their salary if they get at least seven hours of sleep a night. That works out to just over an extra dollar for each night the employee sleeps over seven hours. The idea behind this scheme is employee performance. Human resources oﬃcials say employees will work better if they have slept well. They add that a workforce that is more awake and alert will mean the company will perform better. Staﬀ can either record their sleep automatically using a wrist monitor that connects to Aetna 's computers, or manually record how long they have slept every night. There are a number of studies that warn that not sleeping enough can aﬀect our ability to do our job. The American Academy of Sleep Medicine said that the average worker in the USA loses 11.3 working days of productivity a year because of not getting enough sleep. This costs companies about $2,280 for one worker. It estimates that the US economy loses $63.2 billion a year because workers do not sleep more than seven hours a night. A 2015 study in Europe by the Rand Corporation found that staﬀ who slept less than seven hours per night were far less productive than workers who had eight or more hours of sleep. The staﬀ at Aetna also receive extra cash if they do exercise.
answer: American employees are paid $300 a year to sleep more than seven hours per night and they can record their sleep manually or through an automatic wrist monitor, as sleeping aﬀects daytime performance by inﬂuencing employees’ alertness, which diminish productivity and leads to ﬁnancial loss accumulated to $63.2 billion a year, and similar policies adopted to encourage people taking exercise.(Word count:61)
question_zh: 美国的一家公司付钱给员工，让他们睡得更多。 Aetna 保险公司的员工如果每晚至少睡 7 个小时，每年的工资将增加 300 美元。员工每晚睡眠超过 7 个小时，就相当于多赚了 1 美元多一点。该计划背后的理念是员工绩效。人力资源官员表示，如果员工睡得好，他们会工作得更好。他们补充说，更加清醒和警觉的员工队伍意味着公司会表现得更好。工作人员可以使用连接到 Aetna 计算机的腕式监视器自动记录他们的睡眠，也可以手动记录他们每晚的睡眠时间。许多研究警告说，睡眠不足会影响我们的工作能力。美国睡眠医学会表示，美国平均工人每年因睡眠不足而损失 11.3 个工作日的生产力。公司一名员工的成本约为 2,280 美元。据估计，由于工人每晚睡眠时间不超过 7 小时，美国经济每年损失 632 亿美元。兰德公司 2015 年在欧洲进行的一项研究发现，每晚睡眠时间少于 7 小时的员工的工作效率远低于睡眠时间为 8 小时或以上的员工。安泰保险的员工如果锻炼身体还可获得额外现金。
answer_zh: 美国员工每晚睡眠超过 7 小时，每年可获得 300 美元的报酬，他们可以手动或通过自动手腕监测器记录睡眠情况，因为睡眠会影响员工的警觉性，从而影响白天的表现，从而降低生产力并导致每年累计 632 亿美元的财务损失，并采取类似政策鼓励人们锻炼身体。（字数：61）

question: The feature of being double-blind, where neither patients nor physicians are aware of who receives the experimental treatment, is almost universally trumpeted as being a virtue of clinical trials. Hence, trials that fail to remain successfully double blind are regarded as providing inferior evidential support. The rationale for this view is unobjectionable: doubleb- linding rules out the potentially confounding inﬂuences of patient and physician beliefs. Nonetheless, viewing the double-blind trial as necessarily superior is problematic. For one, it leads to the paradox that very eﬀective experimental treatments will not be supportable by the best evidence. If a new drug were to make even the most severe symptoms of the common cold disappear within seconds, most participants and investigators would correctly identify it as the latest wonder drug and not the control (i.e. placebo) treatment. Any trial testing the eﬀectiveness of this wonder drug will, therefore, fail to remain double-blind. Similar problems arise for treatments, such as exercise and most surgical techniques, whose nature makes them resistant to being tested in double-blind conditions. It seems strange that an account of evidence should make prior judgments that certain claims can never be supported by the best evidence. It would be diﬀerent if the claims at issue were pseudo- scientiﬁc untestable. But so far as treatments with large eﬀects go, the claim that they are eﬀective is highly testable, and intuitively they should receive greater support from the evidence than do claims about treatments with moderate eﬀects.---
answer: Viewing double-blind trial as necessarily superior is problematic, because it can lead to the paradox that very eﬀective experimental treatments will not be supportable by best evidence, and it will cause similar problems for treatments, and as treatments with large eﬀects go, the claim that they are eﬀective is highly testable and intuitively they should receive greater support from the evidence than make claims about treatments with moderate eﬀects.(Word count:69)
question_zh: 双盲的特点，即患者和医生都不知道谁接受了实验性治疗，几乎被普遍吹捧为临床试验的优点。因此，未能成功保持双盲的试验被认为提供了较差的证据支持。这种观点的基本原理是无可非议的：双盲排除了患者和医生信念的潜在混杂影响。尽管如此，将双盲试验视为必然优越是有问题的。其一，它导致了一个悖论：非常有效的实验治疗方法并不能得到最好的证据的支持。如果一种新药能够使最严重的普通感冒症状在几秒钟内消失，大多数参与者和研究人员都会正确地将其识别为最新的神奇药物，而不是对照（即安慰剂）治疗。因此，任何测试这种神奇药物有效性的试验都将无法保持双盲。类似的问题也出现在运动和大多数外科手术等治疗方法中，其性质使其难以在双盲条件下进行测试。似乎很奇怪的是，对证据的说明应该事先判断某些主张永远无法得到最佳证据的支持。如果所涉及的主张是伪科学且无法检验的，情况就会有所不同。但就具有大作用的治疗而言，它们有效的主张是高度可检验的，并且直观地讲，它们应该比具有中等作用的治疗的主张得到更多的证据支持。
answer_zh: 将双盲试验视为必然优越是有问题的，因为它可能会导致一个悖论，即非常有效的实验治疗不会得到最佳证据的支持，并且它会导致治疗出现类似的问题，并且随着具有巨大效果的治疗的进行，声称它们有效的说法是高度可检验的，直观上他们应该比声称具有中等效果的治疗得到更多的证据支持。（字数：69）

question: The evolution of the RAS (Royal Agricultural Society) ﬁts into the broader Western trend of promoting nationalism, progress, and technology through exhibitory venues, which ﬁrst became popular in the 1850s. Various types of fairs, from local agricultural shows to Worlds Fairs, were used as instruments of hegemony to support imperialism, promote burgeoning capitalist endeavors, and shape class identities, social spaces and public spaces Visual culture and the art of display became essential in deﬁning aspects of national distinction. Colonial nations in particular, such as Canada and Australia, were attempting to develop distinct national identities to diﬀerentiate themselves from British imperial power. Agricultural fairs in North America originated at the beginning of the nineteenth century and were devoted to educating practicing framers in ways of improving their cultivation of livestock and crops through the use of various technologies. Symbolically, this cultivation was linked to the colonial project of civilizing wilderness frontiers. By the mid-twentieth century, advertisements in various forms were common and included programs or brochures, which were handed out to fair-goers as they entered. These were seen as opportunities for educating the public. Often comments promoting the importance of the fair were based on ideas about patriotism and nationalism. The Royal Easter Show is a good example of an exhibitory context that grew from a small fair, based on local agricultural competition, to a larger venue that incorporated the mandates of national development and the cultivation of colonial character. In 1822, the RAS was created on the premise that there was a dire need in Australia for the development of improved farming skills to better support growing urban populations and export markets. Organizations based on agricultural improvement which played an integral part in converting and organizing land for colonial purposes.
answer: The evolution of the RAS (Royal Agricultural Society) ﬁts into the broader Western trend of promoting nationalism, progress, and technology through exhibitory venues in the 1850s with fairs supporting imperialism, promoting burgeoning capitalist endeavors, and shaping “class identities, social spaces and public spaces”, and thus Australian organizations based on improved farming skills that better support growing urban populations and export markets played an integral part in converting and organizing land for colonial purpose. (Word count:74 )
question_zh: RAS（皇家农业协会）的发展符合更广泛的西方通过展览场所促进民族主义、进步和技术的趋势，这种趋势在 1850 年代首次流行。从当地农业展览会到世界博览会，各种类型的博览会都被用作霸权的工具，以支持帝国主义，促进新兴的资本主义事业，并塑造阶级身份、社会空间和公共空间。视觉文化和展示艺术在定义民族特征方面变得至关重要。特别是加拿大和澳大利亚等殖民地国家，正试图发展独特的民族认同，以区别于英国的帝国主义势力。北美的农业博览会起源于十九世纪初，致力于教育实践者如何通过使用各种技术来改善牲畜和农作物的种植。具有象征意义的是，这种种植与开化荒野边境的殖民计划有关。到了二十世纪中叶，各种形式的广告很常见，其中包括节目或小册子，在入场者进入时向他们分发。这些被视为教育公众的机会。宣传博览会重要性的评论通常是基于爱国主义和民族主义的思想。皇家复活节展是展览环境的一个很好的例子，它从一个基于当地农业竞争的小型博览会发展成为一个融合了国家发展和殖民特色培育的大型场所。 1822 年，RAS 成立的前提是澳大利亚迫切需要发展改进的农业技能，以更好地支持不断增长的城市人口和出口市场。以农业改良为基础的组织，在为殖民目的转变和组织土地方面发挥了不可或缺的作用。
answer_zh: RAS（皇家农业协会）的演变符合更广泛的西方趋势，即通过 1850 年代的展览场所促进民族主义、进步和技术，其中包括支持帝国主义、促进新兴资本主义事业和塑造“阶级身份、社会空间和公共空间”的展览会，因此，澳大利亚组织以改进的农业技能为基础，更好地支持不断增长的城市人口和出口市场，在为殖民目的转变和组织土地方面发挥了不可或缺的作用。 （字数：74）

question: Slightly less than one in ﬁve carers (19%) were primary carers (475,000 people). That is, they were the main carer of a person who was limited in carrying out the core everyday activities of mobility, communication or self-care. Both primary carers and the larger group of other carers (close to 2 million) contribute to the well-being of older people and people with disabilities. However, because they care for people who otherwise would have diﬃculty carrying out basic everyday activities, there is particular interest in primary carers: in the contribution they make, their well-being, labor force experiences, motivations and the support they receive in caring. Primary carers were more likely than other carers to be assisting someone who lived in the same household (81% compared with 76%). As with caring as a whole, the likelihood of being in primary care increased with age to peak at age 55-64 years, where one in twenty people were primary carers. However, rather than then declining, the likelihood of being a primary carer remained at around this level among the older age groups. Consequently, primary carers had a somewhat older age proﬁle than other carers. The median age of primary carers was 52 years, compared with 47 years for other carers. Primary carers were more likely than other carers to be female (71% compared with 50%) and less likely to be in the labor force (39% compared with 60%). Women not in the labor force were by far the largest single group among primary carers (44%). In contrast, men employed full-time were the largest single group among other carers (25%). Consistent with their lower labor force participation, primary carers had lower personal incomes than other carers (a median gross income of $237 per week compared with $327 per week) and were more likely to have a government pension or allowance as their main source of income (55% compared with 35%).
answer: Slightly less than one in ﬁve carers were primary carers, and both primary carers and the larger group of other carers contribute to the well being of older people and people with disabilities, and there is particular interest in primary carers, and primary carers were more likely than other carers to be assisting someone who lived in the same household, and primary carers had a somewhat older age proﬁle than other carers.
question_zh: 略低于五分之一的护理人员 (19%) 是主要护理人员（475,000 人）。也就是说，他们是一个在行动、交流或自我护理等核心日常活动方面受到限制的人的主要照顾者。主要照顾者和更多的其他照顾者（接近 200 万人）都为老年人和残疾人的福祉做出了贡献。然而，由于初级护理人员照顾的是那些难以进行基本日常活动的人，因此人们对初级护理人员特别感兴趣：他们所做的贡献、他们的福祉、劳动力经验、动机以及他们在护理过程中获得的支持。主要照顾者比其他照顾者更有可能帮助住在同一家庭的人（81% 和 76%）。与整个护理一样，接受初级护理的可能性随着年龄的增长而增加，在 55-64 岁之间达到顶峰，其中二十人中就有一个是初级护理者。然而，在老年群体中，成为主要照顾者的可能性并没有下降，而是保持在这个水平左右。因此，主要照顾者的年龄比其他照顾者稍大一些。主要照顾者的平均年龄为 52 岁，而其他照顾者的平均年龄为 47 岁。与其他护理人员相比，主要护理人员更有可能是女性（分别为 71% 和 50%），而进入劳动力队伍的可能性较小（分别为 39% 和 60%）。迄今为止，非劳动力女性是主要护理人员中最大的单一群体（44%）。相比之下，全职男性是其他护理人员中最大的单一群体（25%）。与劳动力参与率较低相一致的是，主要照顾者的个人收入低于其他照顾者（每周总收入中位数为 237 美元，而每周为 327 美元），并且更有可能将政府养老金或津贴作为主要收入来源（分别为 55% 和 35%）。
answer_zh: 略低于五分之一的护理人员是主要护理人员，主要护理人员和更多的其他护理人员都为老年人和残疾人的福祉做出了贡献，而且人们对主要护理人员特别感兴趣，主要护理人员比其他护理人员更有可能帮助住在同一家庭的人，而且主要护理人员的年龄比其他护理人员稍大一些。

Urbanization has been a deﬁning trend of the modern era, with more than half of the world 's population now living in cities. Cities oﬀer numerous advantages, including access to better job opportunities, healthcare, education, and cultural amenities. The concentration of people and resources in urban areas drives economic growth and innovation, making cities engines of development. Additionally, cities often serve as melting pots of diverse cultures, fostering social integration and the exchange of ideas. However, living in cities also presents several challenges. Urban areas are frequently plagued by issues such as traﬃc congestion, pollution, and high living costs. The dense population can strain infrastructure and public services, leading to problems like inadequate housing and healthcare facilities. Furthermore, cities are often characterized by stark inequalities, with signiﬁcant disparities in wealth and access to resources between diﬀerent neighborhoods. The rapid pace of urbanization can exacerbate these issues, as cities struggle to accommodate the growing population. Sustainability is another critical concern for urban living. High energy consumption and waste generation contribute to environmental degradation and climate change. To address these challenges, urban planners and policymakers are increasingly focusing on creating sustainable, livable cities. This involves promoting public transportation, green spaces, renewable energy sources, and eﬃcient waste management systems. By adopting such measures, cities can enhance the quality of life for their residents while minimizing their environmental impact. Ultimately, while cities oﬀer numerous beneﬁts, they also require careful planning and management to ensure that they remain vibrant, inclusive, and sustainable places to live.
answer: While urbanization has been a trend of the modern era, cities oﬀer access to job opportunities, healthcare, education, and cultural amenities, but they are plagued by issues like traﬃc congestion, pollution, high living costs, stark inequalities in wealth and access to resources, and sustainability concerns, so urban planners and policymakers should focus on creating sustainable livable cities, which means cities require careful planning and management to ensure they remain vibrant, inclusive, and sustainable to live.
question_zh: 城市化已成为现代时代的决定性趋势，目前世界上一半以上的人口居住在城市。城市提供许多优势，包括获得更好的就业机会、医疗保健、教育和文化设施。人口和资源向城市集中，带动经济增长和创新，使城市成为发展的引擎。此外，城市往往是多元文化的熔炉，促进社会融合和思想交流。然而，生活在城市也面临着一些挑战。城市地区经常受到交通拥堵、污染和高生活成本等问题的困扰。人口稠密会给基础设施和公共服务带来压力，导致住房和医疗设施不足等问题。此外，城市往往存在明显的不平等，不同社区之间在财富和资源获取方面存在显着差异。城市化的快速发展可能会加剧这些问题，因为城市正在努力容纳不断增长的人口。可持续性是城市生活的另一个关键问题。高能源消耗和废物产生导致环境退化和气候变化。为了应对这些挑战，城市规划者和政策制定者越来越关注创建可持续、宜居的城市。这包括促进公共交通、绿色空间、可再生能源和高效的废物管理系统。通过采取这些措施，城市可以提高居民的生活质量，同时最大限度地减少对环境的影响。最终，虽然城市提供了众多好处，但它们也需要仔细的规划和管理，以确保它们保持充满活力、包容性和可持续的居住地。
answer_zh: 虽然城市化已成为现代时代的趋势，城市提供了就业机会、医疗保健、教育和文化设施，但它们也受到交通拥堵、污染、高生活成本、财富和资源获取方面的严重不平等以及可持续发展问题等问题的困扰，因此城市规划者和政策制定者应专注于创建可持续的宜居城市，这意味着城市需要仔细的规划和管理，以确保它们保持活力、包容性和可持续的生活。

question: It might seem a little eccentric, but reviewing your work by reading it aloud can help to identify the woolliest areas. This works best if you perform your reading in a theatrical way, pausing at the commas and ends of sentences. If you run out of breath during a sentence, it is probably too long. You ought to be able to convert your writing into a speech in this way if it sounds too stilted and convoluted, perhaps you could rework these parts until they sound ﬂuid. It is unlikely that your reader will be fooled by the idea that long words make you sound clever. Cluttering a sentence with too many complicated words can prevent its meaning from being understood at all. A short word is always preferable to a long one. Why should anyone choose the word erroneous over the word wrong in an essay? Usually, writers who employ more obscure words are trying to sound impressive but can appear pretentious. Direct words enable you to control what you are saying and are not necessarily babyish, but the most appropriate ones for the job. When you read your writing aloud, you will notice that the key stress comes at the end of your sentence. It is, therefore, most eﬀective to end with a short and emphatic word to secure your point. Try to resist the impulse to waﬄe at the end of your sentence by trailing oﬀ into qualifying clauses. It might be worth relocating the clause to the beginning of the sentence or losing it altogether if you feel that it adds little to its meaning. Your sentences might be the most grammatically perfect in the world, but they still, cause your writing to sound wrong if you have misjudged its tone. A colloquial style, which uses slang and exclamations, is an inappropriately chatty tone for an essay. However, style can be equally jarring if your vocabulary is too formal or ambitious for its context. It is much more impressive to make complicated points using simple language and grammar.
answer: It is impressive to make complicated points using simple language and grammar, which includes reviewing by reading aloud to identify the woolliest areas in a theatrical way, pausing at the commas and ends of sentences, preferring short words to long ones that appear pretentious, applying key stress at the end of sentence with a short and emphatic word to secure point, and not misjudging tones between colloquial chatty styles and formal and ambitious context. (Word count:75)
question_zh: 这可能看起来有点奇怪，但通过大声朗读来回顾你的作品可以帮助识别最毛茸茸的区域。如果您以戏剧的方式进行阅读，在逗号和句子结尾处暂停，那么效果最好。如果你在一句话中气喘吁吁，那可能是太长了。你应该能够通过这种方式将你的写作转化为演讲，如果它听起来太生硬和复杂，也许你可以修改这些部分，直到它们听起来流畅。你的读者不太可能被长词让你听起来很聪明的想法所愚弄。句子中包含太多复杂的单词会导致根本无法理解其含义。短词总是比长词好。为什么有人应该在论文中选择“错误”一词而不是“错误”一词？通常，作家使用晦涩难懂的词语是为了让自己听起来令人印象深刻，但可能会显得自命不凡。直接的语言可以让你控制自己所说的话，而且不一定是幼稚的，而是最适合工作的。当你大声朗读你的文章时，你会注意到重音出现在句子的末尾。因此，最有效的方法是用一个简短而有力的词来结束你的观点。试着通过逐渐减弱到限定从句来抑制句子末尾的犹豫冲动。如果您觉得该子句对其含义没有增加什么，则可能值得将该子句重新放置到句子的开头或完全删除它。你的句子可能是世界上语法上最完美的，但如果你误判了它的语气，它们仍然会导致你的写作听起来错误。口语风格使用俚语和感叹词，对于文章来说是一种不恰当的闲聊语气。然而，如果你的词汇对于上下文来说过于正式或过于雄心勃勃，那么风格也可能同样令人不和谐。用简单的语言和语法表达复杂的观点更令人印象深刻。
answer_zh: 使用简单的语言和语法来表达复杂的观点是令人印象深刻的，其中包括通过大声朗读来复习，以戏剧性的方式找出最模糊的部分，在逗号和句子结尾处停顿，喜欢短单词而不是显得自命不凡的长单词，在句子末尾用一个简短而强调的单词强调重音来确保要点，并且不要误判口语闲聊风格与正式和雄心勃勃的上下文之间的语气。 （字数：75）

question: What is museology? A simple deﬁnition might be that it is the study of museums, their history and underlying philosophy, the various ways in which they have, in the course of time, been established and developed, their avowed or unspoken aims and policies, their educative or political or social role. More broadly conceived, such a study might also embrace the bewildering variety of audiences visitors, scholars, art lovers, children -at whom the eﬀorts of museum staﬀ are supposedly directed, as well as related topics such as the legal duties and responsibilities placed upon (or incurred by) museums, perhaps even some thought as to their future. Seen in this light, museology might appear at ﬁrst sight a subject so specialized as to concern only museum professionals, who by virtue of their occupation are more or less obliged to take an interest in it. In reality, since museums are almost, if not quite as old as civilization itself, and since the plethora of present-day museums embraces virtually every ﬁeld of human endeavor - not just art, or craft, or science, but entertainment, agriculture, rural life, childhood, ﬁsheries, antiquities, automobiles: the list is endless - it is a ﬁeld of enquiry so broad as to be a matter of concern to almost everybody.
answer: Museology, the study of museums, which embraces audiences at whom the eﬀorts of museum staﬀ are supposedly directed, might appear as a specialized subject concerning only museum professionals, whose occupation is obliged to take an interest in it, but in reality, since museums are not as old as civilization itself and the plethora of present-day museums embraces every ﬁeld of human endeavor, its list is endless, broad, and a matter of concern to everybody. (Word count:75)
question_zh: 什么是博物馆学？一个简单的定义可能是，它是对博物馆的研究，包括它们的历史和基本哲学、它们随着时间的推移建立和发展的各种方式、它们公开或不言而喻的目标和政策、它们的教育或政治或社会作用。从更广泛的角度来看，这样的研究还可能涵盖令人眼花缭乱的各种观众——参观者、学者、艺术爱好者、儿童——博物馆工作人员的努力据称是针对这些人的，以及相关的主题，例如博物馆所承担的法律义务和责任，甚至可能是对博物馆未来的一些思考。从这个角度来看，博物馆学乍一看似乎是一个如此专业的学科，以至于只涉及博物馆专业人士，他们由于其职业或多或少有义务对它感兴趣。事实上，由于博物馆的历史几乎与文明本身一样古老，甚至与文明本身一样古老，而且由于当今众多的博物馆几乎涵盖了人类努力的每一个领域——不仅是艺术、手工艺或科学，还包括娱乐、农业、乡村生活、童年、渔业、古董、汽车：清单是无穷无尽的——这是一个如此广泛的探究领域，几乎每个人都关心这个问题。
answer_zh: 博物馆学是对博物馆的研究，它的对象是博物馆工作人员的努力所针对的观众，它可能看起来是一门只涉及博物馆专业人员的专门学科，他们的职业有义务对博物馆感兴趣，但实际上，由于博物馆的历史并不像文明本身那么古老，而且当今众多的博物馆涵盖了人类努力的各个领域，因此它的列表是无穷无尽的、广泛的，是每个人都关心的问题。 （字数：75）

question: Major athletic events around the globe from the 2014 Sochi Olympics to an annual powerboat race in Norwegian fjords are striving to neutralize their carbon footprint as part of a worldwide climate network, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) said today. The sporting events are the latest participants to join the network, and are particularly important for inspiring further global action on the environment, said Achim Steiner, UNEP Executive Director. Organizers of the 2014 Sochi Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games to be held in a unique natural setting between the shores of the Black Sea and the soaring snow-capped Caucasus Mountains say they will put an estimated $1.75 billion into energy conservation and renewable energy. That investment will be dedicated to improving transport infrastructure, oﬀsetting greenhouse gas emissions from the use of electricity, air travel and ground transportation, the reforestation of Sochi National Park and the development of green belts in the city.
answer: The United Nations Environment Program( UNEP) said athletic events around the globe are striving to neutralize their carbon footprint as participants in a worldwide climate network, but organizers of the 2014 Sochi Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games say they will invest in energy conservation and renewable energy, dedicating to improving transport infrastructure, oﬀsetting greenhouse gas emissions from air travel and ground transportation, the reforestation of Sochi National Park and the development of green belts.
