In a country where up to 60% of young women are on a diet at any one time, and 70% of school girls say they want to lose weight, despite the fact that most have a normal BMI, such messages are profoundly hazardous to the mental health of young Australians.
answer: Despite a dramatic increase in interest in beauty pageants, where women are judged by their appearance, opponents argue that beauty pageants, which deliver harmful messages to young women, are demeaning to women and symbols of decline in Australia, a country that treats women with dignity and respect. 最新改动：但是文本内容和机经的不是很像 ，先说大家今天的看法认为人就是对女性价值的侮辱 ，大家相信 all come of diﬀerent shapes ，然后说澳洲某某赢过Miss Universal, 但说的意思差不多。然后继续说女生节食不健康 ，等等。 It has been generally believed by present days Australian that both men and women come of diﬀerent shapes and beauty contest may devalue females value, after XX won Miss University in 1941, which has attracted many young women to adopt unhealthy diets to keep slim.
question_zh: 自从澳大利亚选手詹妮弗·霍金斯和劳伦·伊格尔分别加冕环球小姐和国际青少年小姐后，这个国家对选美比赛的兴趣急剧增加。这些胜利还引发了一场争论：选美比赛是否只是对老式价值观的无害提醒，还是对女性因外表而受到尊重的时代的倒退。反对者认为，选美比赛，无论是环球小姐还是国际青少年小姐，都是对女性的侮辱，而且与时代格格不入。他们说它们只不过是衰落的象征。在过去的几十年里，澳大利亚在给予妇女尊严和尊重方面采取了许多步履蹒跚的步骤。年轻女性从小就知道自己可以做任何事，正如 2003 年澳大利亚年度人物菲奥娜·斯坦利教授等鼓舞人心的医学榜样所表明的那样。在 20 世纪 60 年代和 70 年代，女权运动的第一个行动就是对选美比赛进行纠察，前提是选美行业宣扬以外表来评判女性是可以接受的观点。如今，许多年轻的澳大利亚女性仍然对自己的身体形象深感不安，承受着各种压力，因为人们会根据自己的外表来评判她们。几乎所有选美冠军都非常瘦，这强化了“瘦就是美”的信息。这忽略了一个事实：男人和女人有各种身材和体形。在这个国家，高达 60% 的年轻女性在任何时候都在节食，70% 的女学生表示她们想减肥，尽管大多数人的体重指数都正常，此类信息对澳大利亚年轻人的心理健康造成极大危害。

question: Who would have thought back in 1698, as they downed their espressos, that the little band of stockbrokers from Jonathan 's Coﬀee House in Change Alley EC3 would be the founder members of what would become the world 's mighty money capital? Progress was not entirely smooth. The South Sea Bubble burst in 1720, and the coﬀee house exchanges burned down in 1748. As late as the Big Bang in 1986, when bowler hats were ﬁnally hung up, you wouldn 't have bet the farm on London surpassing New York, Frankfurt, and Tokyo as Mammon 's international nexus. Yet the 325,000 souls who operate in the UK capital 's ﬁnancial hub have now overtaken their New York rivals in the size of the funds managed including oﬀshore business they hold 70 of the global secondary bond market and the City dominates foreign exchange trading. And its institutions paid out 9 billion in bonuses in December. The Square Mile has now spread both eastwards from EC3 to Canary Wharf and westwards into Mayfair, where many of the private equity 'locusts ' and their hedge fund pals now hang out. For foreigners in ﬁnance, London is the place to be. It has no Sarbanes Oxley and no euro to hold it back, yet the fact that it still ﬂies so high is against the odds. London is one of the most expensive cities in the world to live in, transport systems groan, and there 's an ever-present threat of terrorist attacks. But, for the time being, the deals just keep on getting bigger.
answer: Despite the humble background and deplorable experience, the high living cost, inferior transport systems and threat of terrorist attack, London have overtaken New York rivals in the funds managed, the global secondary bond market, and foreign exchange trading and become the world’s mighty money capital.
question_zh: 早在 1698 年，当他们喝下浓缩咖啡时，谁会想到来自 Change Alley EC3 乔纳森咖啡馆的一小群股票经纪人会成为后来成为世界强大货币之都的创始人成员？进展并不顺利。南海泡沫于 1720 年破裂，咖啡馆交易所于 1748 年被烧毁。直到 1986 年大爆炸，当圆顶硬礼帽最终挂起时，你也无法打赌伦敦会超越纽约、法兰克福和东京，成为财神的国际枢纽。然而，在英国首都金融中心运营的 325,000 名员工现在在管理的基金规模（包括离岸业务）方面已经超越了纽约的竞争对手，他们持有全球二级债券市场的 70%，而且伦敦金融城在外汇交易中占据主导地位。其机构12月发放奖金90亿。现在，“一平方英里”已经从 EC3 向东延伸至金丝雀码头，并向西延伸至 Mayfair，许多私募股权“蝗虫”和他们的对冲基金伙伴现在都在那里闲逛。对于金融领域的外国人来说，伦敦是一个理想之地。它没有萨班斯·奥克斯利法案，也没有欧元来阻止它，但它仍然飞得如此之高，这一事实是不利的。伦敦是世界上生活成本最昂贵的城市之一，交通系统陷入困境，而且恐怖袭击的威胁始终存在。但就目前而言，交易规模仍在不断扩大。
answer_zh: 尽管出身卑微，经历惨淡，生活成本高昂，交通系统落后，还面临恐怖袭击的威胁，但伦敦在基金管理、全球二级债券市场、外汇交易等方面超越纽约，成为世界强大的货币之都。

question: This year 's Nobel Peace Prize justly rewards the thousands of scientists of the United Nations Climate Change Panel the IPCC. These scientists are engaged in excellent, painstaking work that establishes exactly what the world should expect from climate change. The other award winner, former US Vice President Al Gore, has spent much more time telling us what to fear. While the IPCC 's estimates and conclusions are grounded in careful study, Gore doesn 't seem to be similarly restrained. Gore told the world in his Academy Award- winning movie recently labeled "one-sided " and containing scientiﬁc errors by a British judge to expect 20-foot sea-level rises over this century. He ignores the ﬁndings of his Nobel co- winners, the IPCC, who conclude that sea levels will rise between only a half foot and two feet over this century, with their best expectation being about one foot. That 's similar to what the world experienced over the past 150 years. Likewise, Gore agonizes over the accelerated melting of ice in Greenland and what it means for the planet but overlooks the IPCC 's conclusion that, if sustained, the current rate of melting would add just three inches to the sea level rise by the end of the century. Gore also takes no notice of research showing that Greenlands temperatures were higher in 1941 than they are today. Gore also frets about the future of polar bears. He claims they are drowning as their icy habitat disappears. However, the only scientiﬁc study showing any such thing indicates that four polar bears drowned because of a storm. The politician turned movie maker loses sleep over a predicted rise in heat-related deaths. There 's another side of the story that 's inconvenient to mention rising temperatures will reduce the number of cold spells, which are a much bigger killer than heat. The best study shows that by 2050, heat will claim 400,000 more lives, but 1.8 million fewer will die because of cold. Indeed, according to the ﬁrst complete survey of the economic eﬀects of climate change on the world, global warming will actually save lives.
answer: This year’s Nobel Peace Prize rewards the IPCC scientists and Al Gore, who are engaged in excellent work in climate change, however, Gore expects the sea level to rise 20 feet over this century and worries about the future of polar bears, while the IPCC estimated only a rise of between half a foot and two feet and study shows that the global warming will actually save lives because fewer people will die from cold-related causes.
question_zh: 今年的诺贝尔和平奖公正地奖励了联合国气候变化专门委员会（IPCC）的数千名科学家。这些科学家从事着出色、艰苦的工作，准确确定了世界对气候变化的期望。另一位获奖者、美国前副总统戈尔花了更多的时间告诉我们该害怕什么。虽然政府间气候变化专门委员会的估计和结论是基于仔细的研究，但戈尔似乎并没有同样的克制。戈尔最近在他的奥斯卡获奖电影中告诉全世界，一位英国法官预计本世纪海平面将上升 20 英尺，该电影被贴上了“片面”标签，其中包含科学错误。他忽视了他的诺贝尔奖共同获得者IPCC的调查结果，后者得出的结论是，本世纪海平面只会上升半英尺到两英尺，他们的最佳预期是大约一英尺。这与过去 150 年世界经历的情况类似。同样，戈尔对格陵兰冰层加速融化及其对地球意味着什么感到苦恼，但却忽视了政府间气候变化专门委员会的结论，即如果持续下去，目前的融化速度到本世纪末将使海平面上升仅三英寸。戈尔也没有注意到研究表明 1941 年格陵兰岛的气温比现在高。戈尔还对北极熊的未来感到担忧。他声称，随着冰冷栖息地的消失，它们正在被淹死。然而，唯一表明此类情况的科学研究表明，四只北极熊因暴风雨而淹死。这位从政治家转型为电影制片人的人因预计与高温相关的死亡人数增加而失眠。故事的另一面不方便提及气温上升会减少寒潮的数量，寒潮是比炎热更大的杀手。最好的研究表明，到 2050 年，炎热将导致 40 万人死亡，但死于寒冷的人数将减少 180 万人。事实上，根据对气候变化对世界经济影响的首次全面调查，全球变暖实际上将拯救生命。
answer_zh: 今年的诺贝尔和平奖奖励了在气候变化方面做出杰出工作的IPCC科学家和阿尔·戈尔，然而，戈尔预计本世纪海平面将上升20英尺，并对北极熊的未来感到担忧，而IPCC估计海平面仅上升半英尺到两英尺，研究表明，全球变暖实际上会拯救生命，因为死于寒冷相关原因的人数会减少。

question: Diasporas – communities which live outside, but maintain links with, their homelands – are getting larger, thicker and stronger. They are the human face of globalization. Diaspora consciousness is on the rise: diasporas are becoming more interested in their origins, and organizing themselves more eﬀectively; homelands are revising their opinions of their diasporas as the stigma attached to emigration declines, and stepping up their engagement eﬀorts; meanwhile, host countries are witnessing more assertive diasporic groups within their own national communities, worrying about ﬁfth columns and foreign lobbies, and suﬀering outbreaks of ‘diasporaphobia’ . This trend is the result of ﬁve factors, all of them connected with globalization: the growth in international migration; the revolution in transport and communications technology, which is quickening the pace of diasporans’ interactions with their homelands; a reaction against global homogenized culture, which is leading people to rethink their identities; the end of the Cold War, which increased the salience of ethnicity and nationalism and created new space in which diasporas can operate; and policy changes by national governments on issues such as dual citizenship and multiculturalism, which are enabling people to lead transnational lives. Diasporas such as those attaching to China, India, Russia and Mexico are already big, but they will continue to grow; the migration ﬂows which feed them are likely to widen and quicken in the future.
answer: Diasporas refer to communities living abroad but still maintain close connections with their homelands and this fast-growing phenomenon, occurred in many countries, has posed threats, for example, diasporaphobia to their host countries and this trend is caused by ﬁve factors including the growth in international migration, national policy changes and identify rethinking.(Word count:52)
question_zh: 侨民——居住在国外但与家乡保持联系的社区——正在变得越来越大、越来越稠密、越来越强大。他们是全球化的人性面孔。侨民意识正在兴起：侨民对自己的起源越来越感兴趣，并且更有效地组织自己；随着移民的耻辱感下降，祖国正在改变对海外侨民的看法，并加大参与力度；与此同时，东道国在本国社区内看到了越来越自信的侨民群体，他们担心第五纵队和外国游说团体，并遭受“侨民恐惧症”的爆发。这一趋势是五个因素造成的，所有这些因素都与全球化有关：国际移民的增长；交通和通信技术的革命加快了侨民与祖国互动的步伐；对全球同质化文化的反应，导致人们重新思考自己的身份；冷战的结束增加了种族和民族主义的重要性，并为侨民创造了新的活动空间；各国政府在双重国籍和多元文化等问题上的政策变化，使人们能够过上跨国生活。像中国、印度、俄罗斯和墨西哥这样的海外侨民已经很大，而且还会继续增长；未来，为他们提供食物的移民潮可能会扩大并加速。
answer_zh: 侨民是指居住在国外但仍与祖国保持密切联系的群体，这种快速增长的现象在许多国家发生，对所在国构成了威胁，例如侨民恐惧症，这一趋势是由国际移民增长、国家政策变化和身份重新思考等五个因素造成的。（字数：52）

question: With an abundance of low-priced labor relative to the United States, it is no surprise that China, India and other developing countries specialize in the production of labor-intensive products. For similar reasons, the United States will specialize in the production of goods that are human and physical-capital intensive because of the relative abundance of a highly educated labor force and technically sophisticated equipment in the United States. The division of global production should yield a higher global output of both types of goods than would be the case if each country attempted to produce both of these goods itself. For example, the United States would produce more expensive labor-intensive goods because of its more expensive labor and the developing countries would produce more expensive human and physical capital-intensive goods because of their relative scarcity of these inputs. This logic implies that the United States is unlikely to be a signiﬁcant global competitor in the production of green technologies that are not relatively intensive in human and physical capital. Nevertheless, during the early stages of the development of new technology, the United States had a comparative advantage in the production of the products enabled by this innovation. However, once these technologies become well-understood and production processes are designed that can make use of less-skilled labor; production will migrate to countries with less expensive labor.
answer: The United States will specialize in the production of goods that are human-and-physical capital intensive because of a highly-educated labor force and technically sophisticated equipment, but a logic implies that the United States is unlikely to be a signiﬁcant global competitor in the production green technologies because production will migrate to countries with less expensive labor once technologies become well-understood and production processes are designed that can make use of less-skilled labor. question_zh: 与美国相比，中国、印度等发展中国家拥有丰富的廉价劳动力，因此专门生产劳动密集型产品也就不足为奇了。出于类似的原因，美国将专门生产人力和物质资本密集型商品，因为美国拥有相对丰富的受过高等教育的劳动力和技术先进的设备。全球生产的分工应该会产生比每个国家都试图自己生产这两种商品更高的全球产量。例如，美国将生产更昂贵的劳动密集型产品，因为其劳动力更昂贵，而发展中国家将生产更昂贵的人力和物质资本密集型产品，因为这些投入相对稀缺。这一逻辑意味着，在人力和物质资本相对密集的绿色技术生产领域，美国不太可能成为重要的全球竞争对手。然而，在新技术发展的早期阶段，美国在该创新产品的生产方面具有比较优势。然而，一旦这些技术得到充分理解，并且设计出可以利用技能较低劳动力的生产流程；生产将迁移到劳动力成本较低的国家。
